author: hainho
body:
## 📌 Summary
<!--
    어떤 기능/이슈를 해결했는지 요약해주세요.
-->
round 1 quest의 `회원 가입, 내 정보 조회, 포인트 조회, 포인트 충전 API`의 테스트 코드를 작성하고, 기능을 구현했습니다.
각 API는 별도의 branch로 작업하여 squash and merge 했습니다.

## 💬 Review Points
<!--
    리뷰어가 더 효과적인 리뷰를 할 수 있도록 도와주는 부분입니다.
    (1) 리뷰어가 중점적으로 봐줬으면 하는 부분
    (2) 고민했던 설계 포인트나 로직
    (3) 리뷰어가 확인해줬으면 하는 테스트 케이스나 예외 상황
    (4) 기타 리뷰어가 참고해야 할 사항
-->
각 PR에서 작성한 Review Points를 여기에 정리하면
- 도메인 객체에서 validation을 분리하고 도메인 로직에 집중할 수 있도록 `Value Object`에서 validation을 구현했습니다.
- 테스트 코드에서 반복적인 유저 생성이 필요하여 유저 생성에 대한 로직을 한곳에서 관리하기 위해 `UserFixture`를 구현하여 사용했습니다.
- DTO 사용에 대해서 피드백을 받고, 아래 방식으로 수정하였습니다.
  - 파라미터가 많다고 무조건 하나의 DTO로 묶는 것이 아니라, 비슷한 것들끼리만 묶어서 가독성을 높이는 방향으로 사용
  - DTO를 사용할 때는 의존 방향이 반대가 되지 않도록, 적절한 패키지에 위치 시키기
- 필수 헤더인 `X-USER-ID`가 누락된 경우 400 응답을 줄 수 있도록 `ControllderAdvice`에서 해당 예외를 처리하도록 했습니다.
- Point를 별도의 Entity에 저장할지 User에 저장할지 고민하였으나, 현재 상황에서 별도의 Entity로 분리시킬 이유가 없다고 판단되어 User Entity에 Point를 저장했습니다.

## ✅ Checklist
<!--
    해당 작업이 완료되었는지 확인하기 위한 체크리스트입니다.
    리뷰어가 확인해야 할 사항을 포함합니다.
    계획중이나 아직 완료되지 않은 작업 또한 `TODO -` 로 작성해주세요.  

    ex.
    - [ ] 테스트 코드 포함
    - [ ] 불필요한 코드 제거
    - [ ] README or 주석 보강 (필요 시)
-->
- [x] 테스트 코드 포함
- [x] 불필요한 코드 제거
- [x] README or 주석 보강 (필요 시)
- [x] 회원 가입 구현
- [x] 내 정보 조회 구현
- [x] 포인트 조회 구현
- [x] 포인트 충전 구현

author: luccameds
body:
## 📋 Descrição

Implementação completa do sistema de favoritos para conteúdos, permitindo que usuários marquem e gerenciem seus conteúdos favoritos na plataforma. Esta feature foi desenvolvida seguindo rigorosamente a metodologia **TDD (Test-Driven Development)**.

## 🚀 Funcionalidades Implementadas

### 1. 🗄️ Estrutura de Dados
- **Nova tabela `favorites`** com relacionamento entre usuários e conteúdos
- **Constraints e índices** para garantir integridade e performance
- **Prevenção de duplicatas** através de constraint única
- **Cascading deletes** para manter consistência dos dados

### 2. 🔌 Endpoints da API

#### `POST /api/v1/favorites`
- Adicionar conteúdo aos favoritos
- Validação de autenticação obrigatória
- Verificação de existência do conteúdo
- Tratamento de duplicatas

#### `DELETE /api/v1/favorites/[contentId]`
- Remover conteúdo dos favoritos
- Validação de propriedade do favorito
- Tratamento de favoritos inexistentes

#### `GET /api/v1/user/favorites`
- Listar favoritos do usuário autenticado
- Paginação implementada
- Ordenação por data de criação

### 3. 🔐 Validações e Segurança

- ✅ **Autenticação obrigatória** para todas as operações
- ✅ **Validação de existência** do conteúdo antes de favoritar
- ✅ **Tratamento de duplicatas** com mensagens informativas
- ✅ **Validação de dados** de entrada com schemas específicos
- ✅ **Sanitização de UUIDs** para prevenir injection attacks

### 4. ⚠️ Tratamento de Erros

| Cenário | Status | Mensagem |
|---------|--------|----------|
| **Favorito duplicado** | 400 | "Este conteúdo já está nos seus favoritos." |
| **Conteúdo não encontrado** | 404 | "Conteúdo não encontrado." |
| **Usuário não autenticado** | 401 | "Usuário não autenticado." |
| **Favorito inexistente** | 404 | "Favorito não encontrado." |

## 🛠️ Implementação Técnica

### Arquivos Modificados/Criados

```
📁 infra/migrations/
  └── 1800000000000_add-favorites-table.js    [NEW] Migration da tabela favorites

📁 models/
  ├── favorites/
  │   └── index.js                            [NEW] Modelo de dados dos favoritos
  └── validator.js                            [UPDATED] Novos schemas de validação

📁 pages/api/v1/
  ├── favorites/
  │   ├── index.public.js                     [NEW] POST - Adicionar favorito
  │   └── [contentId]/index.public.js         [NEW] DELETE - Remover favorito
  └── user/favorites/
      └── index.public.js                     [NEW] GET - Listar favoritos do usuário

📁 tests/unit/models/
  └── favorites.test.js                       [NEW] Testes unitários completos
```

### Modelo de Dados (`models/favorites/index.js`)

```javascript
// Principais funcionalidades implementadas:
✅ create()     - Criação com tratamento de duplicatas
✅ remove()     - Remoção com verificação de existência  
✅ findByUser() - Listagem paginada dos favoritos
✅ Validação de schemas com validator
✅ Transações de banco para consistência
```

### Migração de Banco (`1800000000000_add-favorites-table.js`)

```sql
-- Estrutura otimizada com:
✅ Chaves primárias e estrangeiras
✅ Índices para performance (user_id, content_id, created_at)
✅ Constraint única para evitar duplicatas
✅ Timestamps automáticos (created_at)
✅ Cascading deletes para integridade referencial
```

### Extensão do Validator (`models/validator.js`)

```javascript
// Novos schemas adicionados:
✅ createFavoriteSchema - Validação para criação
✅ Validação de UUIDs para user_id e content_id
✅ Sanitização de entrada para prevenir ataques
```

## 🧪 Testes Implementados

- **274 linhas** de testes unitários abrangentes
- **Cobertura completa** de cenários de sucesso e erro
- **Mocks adequados** para isolamento de dependências
- **Testes de validação** e tratamento de erros
- **Testes de edge cases** e cenários limite

### Cenários de Teste Cobertos

```javascript
✅ Criação de favoritos com sucesso
✅ Tratamento de favoritos duplicados
✅ Remoção de favoritos existentes
✅ Tentativa de remoção de favoritos inexistentes
✅ Listagem paginada de favoritos
✅ Validação de dados de entrada
✅ Tratamento de transações de banco
✅ Mocking de dependências externas
```

## 📊 Estatísticas do Commit

```
📈 Commit: a763a25
👤 Autor: Medeiros <luccameds@gmail.com>
📅 Data: Sun Jul 13 22:57:40 2025 -0300

📁 7 arquivos modificados/criados
➕ 817 linhas adicionadas
➖ 1 linha removida
🎯 100% seguindo TDD (Test-Driven Development)
```

## 🔄 Metodologia TDD

Esta implementação seguiu rigorosamente a metodologia **TDD (Test-Driven Development)**:

1. **🔴 Red** - Escrita dos testes primeiro (definição dos requisitos)
2. **🟢 Green** - Implementação mínima para passar nos testes
3. **🔵 Refactor** - Otimização e limpeza do código
4. **✅ Validate** - Garantia de que todos os testes passam

### Benefícios da Abordagem TDD

- **Maior confiabilidade** do código
- **Documentação viva** através dos testes
- **Design orientado pelo uso** da API
- **Facilidade de manutenção** e refatoração
- **Detecção precoce** de bugs e edge cases

## ✅ Checklist de Qualidade

- [x] Testes unitários implementados e passando
- [x] Validação de entrada em todos os endpoints
- [x] Tratamento adequado de erros com mensagens claras
- [x] Documentação clara nas mensagens de erro
- [x] Seguindo padrões do projeto existente
- [x] Migração de banco com rollback implementado
- [x] Índices otimizados para performance
- [x] Autenticação e autorização implementadas
- [x] Constraints de banco para integridade de dados
- [x] Logging adequado para debugging
- [x] Tratamento de transações para consistência
- [x] Validação de UUIDs para prevenir injection

## 🎯 Próximos Passos

Esta implementação fornece uma base sólida e extensível para o sistema de favoritos. Possíveis melhorias futuras:

- [ ] **Cache** para listagem de favoritos populares
- [ ] **Notificações** quando conteúdos favoritados são atualizados
- [ ] **Estatísticas** de favoritos por conteúdo
- [ ] **Exportação** de lista de favoritos
- [ ] **Compartilhamento** de listas de favoritos

## 🔗 Relacionado

- Issue: Implementação da Funcionalidade de Favoritar Postagens #1925
- Tests: `tests/unit/models/favorites.test.js`

Issue #7 の対応として、全プラットフォーム向けのビルドワークフローを追加しました。

### GitHub Actions
- **自動ビルド**: Windows, macOS, Linux, WebGL向けのビルドを自動実行

- **リリース作成**: タグ（v*）プッシュ時に自動的にリリースを作成

### Unity Editor
- ビルド設定メニュー（`uPiper/Build/Configure Build Settings`）
- 全プラットフォーム一括ビルド（`uPiper/Build/Build All Platforms`）
- ビルド前後処理（ONNXモデルの検証、プラットフォーム別設定）

### WebGLデモ
- デモシーンとUIの追加
- テキスト入力と音声生成のUI（実際のTTS実装は後続タスク）

## テスト方法
1. PRマージ後、GitHub Actionsでビルドが実行されることを確認
2. Unity Editorでビルドメニューが動作することを確認
3. WebGLビルドがGitHub Pagesにデプロイされることを確認

author: alohajpm
body:
This PR resolves issue #30706.

Purpose
The primary purpose of this change is to drastically reduce the CI setup time to meet the <20s bounty requirement. The previous Docker-based setup had a best-case time of over 60 seconds, creating a significant bottleneck for all CI jobs.

This PR replaces the Docker environment with a native GitHub Actions runner setup that leverages aggressive caching for both apt and pip dependencies. This significantly speeds up the feedback loop for all developers and makes the CI experience much better.

Changes
Every change in this PR directly contributes to replacing the Docker-based setup with a faster, native one:

.github/workflows/setup/action.yaml: The underlying setup action was completely rewritten. Instead of pulling a Docker image, it now:

Uses awalsh128/cache-apt-pkgs-action to install and cache all required system packages.

Adds necessary build-time libraries (build-essential, portaudio19-dev, libasound-dev, python3-crcmod) to the apt cache list to support Python packages that need to be compiled from source.

Uses the built-in cache: 'pip' feature of actions/setup-python@v4 to efficiently cache all Python dependencies based on the project's pyproject.toml.

.github/workflows/selfdrive_tests.yaml: The main CI workflow was updated to run natively.

The global env variables related to Docker (BASE_IMAGE, RUN, etc.) were removed.

All run steps in the various jobs (build_release, static_analysis, unit_tests, etc.) were modified to execute their commands (scons, pytest, lint.sh) directly on the runner, removing the docker run wrappers.

Verification
These changes were tested and verified through iterative CI runs on this branch.

Initial runs failed due to missing build-time dependencies for packages like crcmod and pyaudio. This was systematically resolved by adding the required development libraries to the apt package list in the setup action.

Subsequent failures related to workflow logic (e.g., Unexpected input 'is_retried') were also fixed.

The final commit passes all CI checks, demonstrating that the new native environment is a complete and functional replacement for the old Docker-based one.

Justification & Benchmarks
This optimization successfully meets the bounty requirement for a sub-20-second setup time.

Before: setup-with-retry stage: ~64 seconds

After (on cache hit): setup-with-retry stage: ~15-18 seconds

This represents a ~75% reduction in the environment setup time. The new setup time can be verified in the GitHub Actions logs for the passing checks on this PR.

body:
> Generated on 2025-07-14 07:33:58 UTC by unknown

## Issue

The application was encountering a `JsonSyntaxException` when deserializing server responses in `TypeAdapters.java`. The exception occurred because the code expected a JSON object, but the server returned a JSON array. This mismatch caused failures in data parsing and prevented the application from functioning as intended.

## Fix

The response model and Retrofit interface were updated to correctly handle a JSON array instead of a single JSON object. The affected method now expects a list of items, aligning with the actual server response format. All relevant handling code was also updated to process a list of objects.

## Details

- Updated the Retrofit interface method to return a list of objects instead of a single object.
- Adjusted the response model and any dependent logic to accommodate a list structure.
- Ensured that deserialization uses the correct type to prevent `JsonSyntaxException`.

## Impact

- Resolves the runtime exception and restores correct data parsing.
- Improves application stability and reliability when processing server responses.
- Ensures future compatibility if the server continues to return arrays.

## Notes

- Further validation of server response formats is recommended to prevent similar issues.
- Additional error handling could be implemented for unexpected response structures.
- No changes were made to server-side code; all fixes are client-side.

## All Exceptions

- **JsonSyntaxException: Expected a JsonObject but was JsonArray**
  - **File:** TypeAdapters.java
  - **Line:** 1010
  - **Exception Details:** com.google.gson.JsonSyntaxException: Expected a com.google.gson.JsonObject but was com.google.gson.JsonArray; at path $
  - **Cause:** The server response is a JSON array, but the code expects a JSON object. This mismatch causes Gson to throw a JsonSyntaxException during deserialization.
  - **Fix:** Updated the Retrofit interface and model classes to match the actual JSON structure returned by the server. The response model now expects a List or an array, not a single object. Handling code was updated to process a list of tasks instead of a single task object.

body:
## 🎨 Color Palette Modernization

This PR completely modernizes the portfolio's color scheme, replacing the dated bright yellow palette with sophisticated amber tones that maintain the yellow/black theme while providing a professional, contemporary 2025 aesthetic.

### Key Changes

**Before (Old Palette):**
- Bright, neon-like yellows (`#f5e269`, `#dfc412`) that felt dated
- Inconsistent red accents (`#ca3131`) that didn't fit the theme
- Brownish text colors (`#414033`) with limited contrast options

**After (Modern Palette):**
- **Primary Amber**: `#D97706` - Rich, sophisticated base color
- **Medium Amber**: `#F59E0B` - Balanced highlight tone  
- **Light Amber**: `#FCD34D` - Gentle accent color
- **Deep Amber**: `#B45309` - Strong contrast accent
- **Modern Typography**: `#1F2937`, `#374151` - Contemporary grays
- **Warm Backgrounds**: `#FFFBEB`, `#FEF3C7` - Subtle yellow-tinted surfaces

### Accessibility Excellence ♿

All color combinations have been tested and meet **WCAG AA accessibility standards**:
- Primary text on background: **14.16** contrast ratio ✓ AAA
- Secondary text combinations: **9.94+** contrast ratio ✓ AAA  
- Button text on amber: **5.02** contrast ratio ✓ AA
- Form elements: **4.66+** contrast ratio ✓ AA

### Files Updated

- `styles/globalstyled.tsx` - Core theme object and global styles
- `styles/styledCommon.ts` - Common components (buttons, titles)
- `styles/contactstyle.ts` - Contact form styling
- `styles/projectsstyle.ts` - Project pages and layouts
- `styles/slugstyle.ts` - Blog post styling

### Visual Impact

![Modernized Portfolio Contact Page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ab074dc-6327-46ce-943c-9e0c1acdf92c)

The transformation showcases:
- Professional amber button styling with proper hover states
- Clean, modern typography with excellent readability
- Consistent warm backgrounds that feel contemporary
- Elegant form styling with improved focus states

### Design Benefits

✅ **Professional Appeal** - Sophisticated amber tones vs bright neon yellows  
✅ **Modern Aesthetic** - Follows 2025 design trends with warm, accessible colors  
✅ **Theme Consistency** - Unified yellow/amber palette, eliminated inconsistent reds  
✅ **Accessibility** - All combinations exceed WCAG standards for inclusive design  
✅ **Brand Cohesion** - Maintains yellow/black identity while feeling contemporary  

This modernization preserves the original design intent while bringing the portfolio's visual identity into 2025 with a refined, professional appearance.

Fixes #18.

author: priscillatrevizan
body:
# Resumo da Atualização: Suporte a Fundos de Investimento

Este pull request adiciona suporte completo à gestão e transações com **fundos de investimento** no backend. As principais atualizações incluem mudanças no schema do banco de dados, inclusão de dados mock, aprimoramentos na API e ajustes na lógica de transações.

## Melhorias no Banco de Dados e Schema

- Adicionado novo modelo `FundInvestment` ao `schema.prisma`, com os seguintes campos:
  - `id`
  - `name`
  - `type`
  - `description`
  - `rate`
  - `rateType`
  - `minimumInvestment`
  - relacionamento com transações associadas

- Modelo `Transaction` atualizado para incluir relação com `FundInvestment` através do campo `fundInvestmentId`.

## Seeding e Dados Mock

- Criado arquivo `funds-mock.json` com dados fictícios de fundos de investimento.
- Atualizado o script `seed.js` para:
  - Limpar dados existentes
  - Ler o novo mock
  - Popular a tabela `FundInvestment` com os fundos de exemplo

## Aprimoramentos na API

- Endpoints adicionados:
  - `GET /funds`: lista todos os fundos de investimento
  - `GET /funds/:id`: retorna detalhes de um fundo específico
  - Os fundos agora também são incluídos na resposta do endpoint `GET /assets`

- Rotas de transações com fundos:
  - `POST /buy-fund`: compra de fundo
  - `POST /sell-fund`: venda de fundo

## Atualizações na Lógica de Transações

- A função `handleBuyTransaction` foi estendida para suportar compras de fundos, incluindo:
  - Validação de entrada
  - Cálculo de valor total
  - Registro da transação

- Nova função `venderFundo` implementada para processar vendas de fundos, incluindo:
  - Cálculo de impostos
  - Atualização da conta de investimento
  - Criação de registros de movimentação e transação

## Melhorias Adicionais

- Tratamento de autenticação aprimorado: a variável `JWT_SECRET` agora é obrigatória no ambiente.
- A função `getContasByUser` foi atualizada para priorizar usuários autenticados e garantir que a resposta seja sempre um array, mesmo em casos de erro ou ausência de contas.

---

Essas mudanças tornam o sistema backend apto a realizar operações completas com fundos de investimento, ampliando as possibilidades de investimento da aplicação.

### kernel: x86/microcode/AMD: Fix out-of-bounds on systems with CPU-less NUMA nodes
[CVE-2025-21991](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-21991)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

x86/microcode/AMD: Fix out-of-bounds on systems with CPU-less NUMA nodes

Currently, load_microcode_amd() iterates over all NUMA nodes, retrieves their
CPU masks and unconditionally accesses per-CPU data for the first CPU of each
mask.

According to Documentation/admin-guide/mm/numaperf.rst:

  "Some memory may share the same node as a CPU, and others are provided as
  memory only nodes."

Therefore, some node CPU masks may be empty and wouldn't have a "first CPU".

On a machine with far memory (and therefore CPU-less NUMA nodes):
- cpumask_of_node(nid) is 0
- cpumask_first(0) is CONFIG_NR_CPUS
- cpu_data(CONFIG_NR_CPUS) accesses the cpu_info per-CPU array at an
  index that is 1 out of bounds

This does not have any security implications since flashing microcode is
a privileged operation but I believe this has reliability implications by
potentially corrupting memory while flashing a microcode update.

When booting with CONFIG_UBSAN_BOUNDS=y on an AMD machine that flashes
a microcode update. I get the following splat:

  UBSAN: array-index-out-of-bounds in arch/x86/kernel/cpu/microcode/amd.c:X:Y
  index 512 is out of range for type 'unsigned long[512]'
  [...]
  Call Trace:
   dump_stack
   __ubsan_handle_out_of_bounds
   load_microcode_amd
   request_microcode_amd
   reload_store
   kernfs_fop_write_iter
   vfs_write
   ksys_write
   do_syscall_64
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe

Change the loop to go over only NUMA nodes which have CPUs before determining
whether the first CPU on the respective node needs microcode update.

  [ bp: Massage commit message, fix typo. ]

#### Severity
Moderate

#### References

- [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2356917](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2356917)

### kernel: nvme-tcp: fix potential memory corruption in nvme_tcp_recv_pdu()
[CVE-2025-21927](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-21927)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvme-tcp: fix potential memory corruption in nvme_tcp_recv_pdu()

nvme_tcp_recv_pdu() doesn't check the validity of the header length.
When header digests are enabled, a target might send a packet with an
invalid header length (e.g. 255), causing nvme_tcp_verify_hdgst()
to access memory outside the allocated area and cause memory corruptions
by overwriting it with the calculated digest.

Fix this by rejecting packets with an unexpected header length.

#### Severity
Important

### kernel: iscsi_ibft: Fix UBSAN shift-out-of-bounds warning in ibft_attr_show_nic()
[CVE-2025-21993](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-21993)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iscsi_ibft: Fix UBSAN shift-out-of-bounds warning in ibft_attr_show_nic()

When performing an iSCSI boot using IPv6, iscsistart still reads the
/sys/firmware/ibft/ethernetX/subnet-mask entry. Since the IPv6 prefix
length is 64, this causes the shift exponent to become negative,
triggering a UBSAN warning. As the concept of a subnet mask does not
apply to IPv6, the value is set to ~0 to suppress the warning message.

#### Severity
Moderate

[CVE-2024-53104](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-53104)

<details>

#### Details
A vulnerability was found in the Linux kernel's USB Video Class driver. A buffer for video frame data is allocated, which does not account for all of the frame formats contained in a video stream, leading to an out-of-bounds write when a stream includes frames with an undefined format. An attacker who is able to influence the format of video streams captured by a system's USB video device could exploit this flaw to alter system memory and potentially escalate their privileges or execute arbitrary code.

body: Previously this was shadowing the user's cwd path onto the device, e.g. if you were installing from `/home/foo/bar` it would create `/home/foo/bar/PublicStaging` on the device. For uniformity with other tools like `ideviceinstaller`, clean this up and just create `/PublicStaging`.

author: jeadie
body:
## 📝 Summary
- This PR reenables several full text search tests. It also updates snapshots where needed and has several bug fixes. 

### Bug 1: Type Hints for FTS UDTF
 - Tantivy has more coarse types than Apache Arrow. As such, there can be schema mismatch problems when converting back into Arrow types (e.g. a table with primary key int32, would recevied int64 from its FTS index). To resolve this, the FTS index is created with type hints from the dataset associated to it.
 - The schema returned via the UDTF `TableProvider` did not propagate these type hints.

### Bug 2: Column type in UDTF
 - `text_search(catalog_page, 'In general basic', cp_description)` was incorrectly trying to parse the optional column argument as a string literal, instead of a column.

author: kwsantiago
body:
Fixes https://github.com/bennyhodl/dlcdevkit/issues/95

## Problem
Slow PostgreSQL queries (>1s) when fetching contract data due to 2MB rows with large BYTEA fields mixed with frequently queried metadata.

## Solution
Split the contracts table into separate metadata and data tables to optimize query performance.

## Changes
- **Migration 0004**: Creates `contract_metadata` and `contract_data` tables
- **Index**: Added `idx_contract_metadata_state` for faster state filtering
- **Storage**: Updated all PostgreSQL storage methods to use split tables
- **Safety**: Preserves existing data and includes rollback migration

## Files Modified
- `src/storage/postgres/migrations/0004_split_contract_tables.{up,down}.sql`
- `src/storage/sqlx.rs` - Added new table structs
- `src/storage/postgres/mod.rs` - Updated storage implementation

## Expected Performance
Query times should improve from >1s to <100ms by only loading metadata when contract data isn't needed.

author: copilot
body:
This PR refactors the `DomNode` and `VDomNode` classes to improve code organization, reduce coupling, and enhance maintainability by implementing clear separation of concerns.

## Changes Made

### 1. Created VDomTraversal Utility Class (`src/vdom/vdom-traversal.ts`)
Extracted all static traversal methods from `VDomNode` into a dedicated utility class:
- `preOrderTraversal()` - Tree traversal in pre-order
- `findLowestCommonAncestor()` - Find common ancestor between nodes
- `determineLeftRight()` - Determine left-right order of nodes
- `findVDomNodesBetween()` - Find nodes between two boundaries
- `traversalAfterPath()` - Traverse nodes after a given path
- `traversalBeforePath()` - Traverse nodes before a given path

### 2. Created DomVDomConverter Utility Class (`src/vdom/dom-vdom-converter.ts`)
Extracted conversion logic between DOM and VDom into a dedicated converter:
- `fromHtmlElement()` - Convert HTMLElement to VDomNode
- `fromVDomNode()` - Convert VDomNode to DomNode
- `buildDomTree()` - Build complete DOM tree from VDom tree

### 3. Refactored DomNode Class
**Removed responsibilities:**
- VDomNode dependency and imports
- Static conversion methods (`from()`, `fromVdom()`)

**Focused on core DOM responsibilities:**
- DOM element management with singleton pattern
- Factory methods for creating DOM elements
- Text formatting and content management
- Tree manipulation (attach, detach, absorb)

### 4. Refactored VDomNode Class
**Removed responsibilities:**
- Static traversal methods (moved to `VDomTraversal`)
- DOM conversion methods (moved to `DomVDomConverter`)

**Focused on virtual DOM responsibilities:**
- Virtual tree structure management
- Hash-based equality and comparison
- Text content and formatting for virtual nodes
- Deep cloning for state management

### 5. Updated Dependencies
- Updated `Synchronizer` to use new converter classes
- Updated command handlers (`DeleteHandler`, `ShortcutFormat`) to use `VDomTraversal`
- Updated all test files to use new utility classes
- Fixed all imports and references

## Benefits

✅ **Better separation of concerns** - Each class has a single, well-defined responsibility  
✅ **Reduced coupling** - DomNode and VDomNode no longer depend on each other  
✅ **Improved maintainability** - Utility classes make code easier to understand and modify  
✅ **Enhanced reusability** - Traversal and conversion logic can be reused independently  
✅ **Cleaner API** - Classes have focused, predictable interfaces  

## Testing

- All builds pass successfully
- 51/55 tests pass (4 failing tests are unrelated to this refactoring - they're DOM environment issues)
- UI functionality verified working correctly

![Application Screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27308d37-e1cd-4d05-8c1c-924c92a60cc8)

The editor continues to work as expected with text input, formatting, and all core functionality intact.

Fixes #11.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The CI workflow was encountering multiple critical errors across several runs:

1. **Syntax Error**: `coordinator.py` had a corrupted line 87 with mixed incompatible code causing parse failures
2. **Formatting Issues**: Multiple files failed black and isort checks
3. **Test Failures**: Tests were failing due to improper async mock usage
4. **Import Issues**: Unused imports causing linting violations

## Root Cause

The `coordinator.py` file appeared to have been corrupted with conflicting implementations - it contained both a simple binary server-based coordinator and incompatible aioAnyList library code mixed together, resulting in:

```python
# Line 87 had invalid syntax like this:
return await self._async_update_internal()            from aiohttp import ClientSession
```

## Solution

### 1. **Fixed Critical Syntax Error**
- Completely cleaned up `coordinator.py` by removing 170+ lines of corrupted aioAnyList code
- Kept only the working binary server implementation that matches the integration's architecture
- Restored proper class structure and method implementations

### 2. **Applied Code Formatting Standards**
- Ran `black` formatting on all Python files
- Applied `isort` import sorting to organize imports consistently
- Removed unused import (`homeassistant.helpers.config_validation as cv`) from `config_flow.py`

### 3. **Fixed Test Infrastructure**
- Updated `test_init.py` to use `AsyncMock` instead of `Mock` for async functions
- Fixed the `TypeError: object bool can't be used in 'await' expression` error

### 4. **Improved CI Configuration**
- Removed `continue-on-error: true` flags from formatting and test steps
- This ensures the CI properly fails when there are actual issues

## Validation

All CI workflow steps now pass successfully:

- ✅ **Black formatting**: All 7 files properly formatted
- ✅ **Import sorting**: All imports organized correctly
- ✅ **Syntax checking**: Zero critical syntax errors (E9,F63,F7,F82)
- ✅ **Code linting**: Zero linting violations
- ✅ **Tests**: All 2 tests passing
- ✅ **Manifest validation**: JSON structure is valid

## Files Changed

- `custom_components/anylist/coordinator.py` - Major cleanup (removed corrupted code)
- `custom_components/anylist/__init__.py` - Formatting improvements
- `custom_components/anylist/config_flow.py` - Removed unused import, formatting
- `custom_components/anylist/intent.py` - Formatting improvements
- `custom_components/anylist/todo.py` - Formatting improvements
- `tests/test_init.py` - Fixed async mock usage
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` - Removed continue-on-error flags

This ensures the integration maintains its intended functionality (binary server-based AnyList integration) while meeting all code quality standards.

> The CI workflow for the repository is encountering multiple errors across several runs. These errors need to be diagnosed and resolved to ensure the workflow completes successfully. Steps required to fix the errors include:
> 
> 1. Identify the cause of the errors in the CI workflow logs.
> 2. Update the workflow configuration or repository code as needed to address these issues.
> 3. Test the fixes to confirm the workflow runs successfully without errors.
> 
> Actions to address the problems may include correcting syntax errors, updating dependencies, or modifying the test cases causing failures. The fixes should be applied in a way that maintains the integrity and functionality of the repository.

body: **Motivation** - this is a precondition for #7860 - when publishing a block, we need to ensure we have enough peers on all column subnets so that we can publish all blobs data to the network - this is not a concern for a node without validator but since this is very easy to achieve, we don't need to care this case **Description** - track `samplingGroups` on PeerData - for sampling groups, ensure at least 6 per subnets - for non-sampling groups, ensure at least 4 per subnets **Metrics on fusaka-devnet-2** we have 25-35 peers on all subnets, so this is more than enough

author: anjato
body:
Changes introduce comprehensive support for crafting Dragon Leather alongside significant improvements to the overall crafting configuration.

- **Dragon Leather Crafting:** Added full support for crafting green, blue, red, and black dragonhide armour pieces (vambraces, chaps, body).
- **Enhanced Configuration:** Updated the crafting configuration system to be more dynamic, allowing scripts to display their current states and additional properties (e.g., number of items created).
- **ICraftingScript Interface:** Introduced `ICraftingScript` to standardize dynamic config handling across all crafting scripts.
- **Script Adaptations:** Refactored all existing crafting scripts to implement the new `ICraftingScript` interface, ensuring compatibility and consistency.
- **Dedicated Config Options:** Added a new configuration dropdown specifically for the Dragon Leather script.
- **Fixed some IDE warnings:** Fixed a few IDE warnings along with a couple of deprecated method calls in the existing crafting scripts. Core functionality was not changed in existing scripts.

body: The `create_default_school_data` function was failing because it was running with the permissions of the user who created the school, and you did not have permissions to insert into the `subjects` table. This change modifies the function to run with `SECURITY DEFINER` to ensure that it has the necessary permissions to insert the default data.

author: lshaowei18
body: > [!IMPORTANT] > 👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._ ## Problem Closes #29397 ## Changes When transforming columns, we replace `person` by using the `personDisplayNameProperties`. This references https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/31704 for its implementation although the code is written in python and for backend. I added a `-- Person` behind as well if there isn't any comment, so that it can eventually be displayed nicely if https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/34948 gets through. ## Did you write or update any docs for this change? - [x] No docs needed for this change ## How did you test this code? Locally, to reproduce: 1) Go to a survey with results 2) Click on export -> export current columns -> csv 3) Download the exported file 4) You should see that the person's column is no longer `person.properties.email`, but a long `coalesce`, and the rows that you see should match what you have on the UI. (Previously, it will only have emails, so if your row has `distinct_id` it wouldn't show.

### Debugging Code Removal:
* Removed `console.log` statements used for debugging in `TransfersPage.tsx` to clean up the code. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3670b34afd1c75b08784a3ea0a5a75729983dff16f8890a054ac24b6c1102092L313) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3670b34afd1c75b08784a3ea0a5a75729983dff16f8890a054ac24b6c1102092L828) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3670b34afd1c75b08784a3ea0a5a75729983dff16f8890a054ac24b6c1102092L879-L880)

### Vehicle Part Association Logic Enhancements:
* Introduced logic to dynamically fetch the associated vehicle type based on `vehicleId` in `VehiclePartFormModal.tsx`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9203038a8dc682a6ab1471ebb6632eba65e91245d887b28341dbf7093168ba33R57-R58) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9203038a8dc682a6ab1471ebb6632eba65e91245d887b28341dbf7093168ba33L65-R67)
* Modified conditional rendering in `VehiclePartFormModal.tsx` to ensure certain form fields are displayed only when creating a new vehicle part. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9203038a8dc682a6ab1471ebb6632eba65e91245d887b28341dbf7093168ba33L264-R266) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9203038a8dc682a6ab1471ebb6632eba65e91245d887b28341dbf7093168ba33L281-R284) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9203038a8dc682a6ab1471ebb6632eba65e91245d887b28341dbf7093168ba33L306-R308)
* Added support for associating and disassociating vehicle parts with headquarters and vehicles in `VehiclePartsPage.tsx`.

### Inventory Table UI Updates:
* Enhanced the `EditableInventorySubTable` component in `VehiclePartInventorySubTable.tsx` with new features:
  - Added vehicle association and disassociation actions.
  - Improved modal functionality for associating/disassociating vehicles.
  - Updated table columns to include vehicle information and refined action buttons.

### API Integration Updates:
* Updated the `saveInventoryRow` function in `VehiclePartsPage.tsx` to support vehicle association via query parameters.
* Added the `associatedVehiclePart` function to handle API calls for associating/disassociating vehicle parts.

### Other Minor Changes:
* Removed unused imports and cleaned up code in `VehiclePartsPage.tsx`.
* Adjusted the `VehiclePartPayload` interface to remove outdated comments and ensure consistency.

- Updated package.json to include Spotlight.js as a dependency and added a new script for development.

  * Enabled React Strict Mode for improved development checks.

author: oncsr
body:
# 🚀 Algorithm_second 2주차 [권혁준]

## 📌 문제 풀이 개요
- 이번 PR에서는 다음 5문제의 풀이를 포함합니다.
- 각 문제에 대한 풀이 과정과 접근 방식을 설명합니다.
---

## ✅ 문제 해결 여부

  - [x] **병약한 윤호**
  - [x] **백도어**  
  - [x] **상어 초등학교**
  - [x] **목장 건설하기**  
  - [x] **좋은 친구**  
  
---

## 💡 풀이 방법
### 문제 1: 병약한 윤호

**문제 난이도**

Gold 5

**문제 유형**

- BFS

**접근 방식 및 풀이**

고유 상태를 2차원으로 정의했습니다.
(l, r) = 왼쪽에서 l개, 오른쪽에서 r개 먹은 경우

(0, 3N+1)에서 시작하는 BFS를 돌려 해결했습니다.

BFS 대신 DP로도 해결할 수 있어 보입니다.

---


### 문제 2: 백도어

**문제 난이도**

Gold 5

**문제 유형**

- 다익스트라

**접근 방식 및 풀이**

기본적인 다익스트라로 해결했습니다.

답이 int범위를 넘을 수 있어서 long 자료형을 사용해야 합니다.

--


### 문제 3: 상어 초등학교

**문제 난이도**

Gold 5

**문제 유형**

- 구현

**접근 방식 및 풀이**

문제에서 제시된 대로, 학생을 배치할 2차원 배열을 만들었습니다.

이후 주어지는 학생을 순서대로 우선순위에 맞게 처리했습니다.

여기서 저는 각 학생이 좋아하는 학생들을 `비트마스킹`으로 관리했었는데, 학생 수가 많아 Integer 범위 내에 다 들어오지 않아서 틀렸었습니다.
이걸 다시 2차원 배열로 고쳐서 해결했습니다.

---


### 문제 4: 목장 건설하기

**문제 난이도**

Gold 4

**문제 유형**

- 누적 합
- 매개 변수 탐색

**접근 방식 및 풀이**

한 변의 길이가 x인 정사각형이 만약 목장 내에 존재한다면, 변의 길이가 x 이하인 모든 정사각형 또한 존재합니다.
이 사실을 이용해서, 이분 탐색으로 정답을 찾아줬습니다.

이 때, 어떤 정사각형 내에 나무나 바위가 존재하는지 빠르게 알아내기 위해 이차원 누적 합을 활용했습니다.

---


### 문제 5: 좋은 친구

**문제 난이도**

Gold 4

**문제 유형**

- 누적 합
- 슬라이딩 윈도우

**접근 방식 및 풀이**

2차원 배열 `a[i][j] = 첫 번째 단어부터 i번째 단어까지 길이가 j인 단어의 개수`을 정의했습니다.

이 배열을 누적 합으로 채워준 뒤에 답을 구할 때는 구간 길이를 K로 두고 슬라이딩 윈도우로 배열 a를 훑으며 구해줬습니다.

body: > [!IMPORTANT] > Adds experimental feature to make all textual elements interactable, controlled by a new setting in `config.py`, with changes in `domUtils.js` and `page.py`. > > - **Behavior**: > - Introduces `ENABLE_EXP_ALL_TEXTUAL_ELEMENTS_INTERACTABLE` in `config.py` to control experimental feature. > - In `domUtils.js`, sets `window.GlobalEnableAllTextualElements` to `false` by default, making all textual elements interactable if set to `true`. > - Modifies `buildElementTree()` in `domUtils.js` to force textual elements to be interactable when the global flag is enabled. > - **Integration**: > - Updates `SkyvernFrame.create_instance()` in `page.py` to set `window.GlobalEnableAllTextualElements` based on the new setting. > - Replaces direct `settings` access with `SettingsManager.get_settings()` in `page.py` for configuration values. > - **Misc**: > - Adds comments and minor refactoring in `domUtils.js` for clarity. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=Skyvern-AI%2Fskyvern&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for af6681890dcb4c5680ccebda9aa4ac6d5fb84cfd. author: hffp
body:
## PR Scope

fix(v4): correct domain.name casing in getPermitData

## Description

This PR corrects the casing of the `domain.name` field returned by `V4PositionManager.getPermitData` from **"Uniswap V4 Positions NFT"** to **"Uniswap v4 Positions NFT"**, aligning it with the actual contract deployment and EIP-712 signature verification expectations.

This change ensures consistent behavior with frontend and signature validation tools that depend on exact string casing.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- Manually verified the `getPermitData` output
- Confirmed that EIP-712 signatures now match the domain used in production

## Are there any breaking changes?

No breaking changes.

author: dd32
body:
Various blocks are made available through the site editor, such as on WordCamp.

These mean the block can be previewed, which may generate warnings such as this:

```
E_WARNING Undefined array key "postId"
URL  https://example.wordcamp.org/2025/wp-json/wp/v2/block-renderer/wporg/favorite-button?context=edit&attributes%5BshowCount%5D=false&attributes%5Bvariant%5D=default&_locale=user
File  pub-sync/blocks/favorite-button/render.php:10
```

Whether these blocks should be presented for insertion is one thing, but avoiding the warning and returning nothing would be nice.

author: alexxa
body:
These tests ensure:
 - the installed RHUI client rpm matches the VM offer
 - exactly one RHUI client rpm is installed
 - the expected RHUI certificate file exists.
 - the RHUI certificate is valid for at least 10 weeks from the current date

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce helper functions and tests to validate that the correct Azure RHUI client package is installed for the VM offer and that the corresponding RHUI certificate is present and valid for at least ten weeks.

New Features:
- Add helper functions to compute expected RHUI client RPM and certificate names based on RHEL release and Azure VM offer

Tests:
- Add test to verify exactly one RHUI client RPM is installed and matches the VM's offer
- Enhance RHUI certificate test to use computed certificate name and ensure it exists and remains valid for at least 10 weeks

body:
**Important:** *Do not tick a checkbox if you haven’t performed its action.* Honesty is indispensable for a smooth review process.

_In the following questions `<cask>` is the token of the cask you're submitting._

After making any changes to a cask, existing or new, verify:

- [ ] The submission is for [a stable version](https://docs.brew.sh/Acceptable-Casks#stable-versions) or [documented exception](https://docs.brew.sh/Acceptable-Casks#but-there-is-no-stable-version).
- [ ] `brew audit --cask --online <cask>` is error-free.
- [ ] `brew style --fix <cask>` reports no offenses.

Additionally, **if adding a new cask**:

- [ ] Named the cask according to the [token reference](https://docs.brew.sh/Cask-Cookbook#token-reference).
- [ ] Checked the cask was not [already refused](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3AHomebrew%2Fhomebrew-cask+is%3Aclosed+is%3Aunmerged+&type=pullrequests) (add your cask's name to the end of the search field).
- [ ] `brew audit --cask --new <cask>` worked successfully.
- [ ] `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API=1 brew install --cask <cask>` worked successfully.

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/SravandeepReddy2004/skills-introduction-to-repository-management/security/code-scanning/1](https://github.com/SravandeepReddy2004/skills-introduction-to-repository-management/security/code-scanning/1)

To address this issue, we will replace the SHA-256 password hashing with a strong, modern password hashing algorithm, such as Argon2. The `argon2-cffi` library provides an implementation of Argon2, which supports both hashing and verification of passwords. The new implementation will include the following:

1. Replace the `hash_password` function to use Argon2 for hashing passwords.
2. Add a validation function using Argon2 to verify hashed passwords during login.
3. Install the `argon2-cffi` library as it is not currently imported.
4. Update the `login` function to use the Argon2 password verification instead of comparing plaintext hashes.

author: jangamkeerthi26
body:
This PR introduces the /api/flights POST endpoint to enable flight search functionality via API. It includes request validation, dynamic pricing calculation, and seat availability filtering based on the given input parameters.
### Key Features
- POST /api/flights endpoint under Api::FlightsController
- FlightSearchValidator:
  - Validates presence of source, destination, and date
  - Ensures source and destination are different
- FlightSearchService:
  - Filters matching flights from data.txt based on source, destination, date, class type, and seat availability
  - Uses dynamic pricing via DynamicPricingService
  - Skips past flights if the requested date is today and time has already passed
- Proper error handling for invalid inputs (`400 Bad Request`)
- JSON response format:
  - Success: list of available flights and a success message
  - Failure: error messages with 400 status
### API Usage Example
**POST /api/flights**
{
  "source": "Bangalore",
  "destination": "London",
  "date": "2025-07-15",
  "class_type": "economy",
  "passengers": 1
}

## Contributing Guidelines

We have prepared a `pre-commit` hook to enforce consistent code formatting across the project. If your code complies with the standards, you should not see any errors, you can clean up your code following the steps below:

1. Install the required dependencies:

```shell
    pip install ruff pre-commit
```

2. Then, run the following command before commit:

```shell
    pre-commit run --all-files
```

3. Finally, please double-check your code to ensure it complies with the following additional specifications as much as possible:
  - Avoid hard-coding local paths: Make sure your submissions do not include hard-coded local paths, as these paths are specific to individual development environments and can cause compatibility issues. Use relative paths or configuration files instead.
  - Clear error handling: Implement clear error-handling mechanisms in your code so that error messages can accurately indicate the location of the problem, possible causes, and suggested solutions, facilitating quick debugging.
  - Detailed comments and documentation: Add comments to complex code sections and provide comprehensive documentation to explain the functionality of the code, input-output requirements, and potential error scenarios.

Thank you for your contributions!

author: kevinjdonohue
copilot
body:
Railway deployments were failing with the error:

```
Error: Cannot find module '@vscode/test-web'
Require stack:
- /app/scripts/railway-vscode-server.mjs
```

The issue occurred because `@vscode/test-web` was listed in `devDependencies` but is required at runtime by the VS Code web server script. Railway's production build process uses `--omit=dev` flags, which excludes devDependencies from installation.

## Changes Made

- **package.json**: Moved `@vscode/test-web` from devDependencies to dependencies
- **Dockerfile**: Simplified npm install command to use standard dependency resolution instead of manual package specification

## Root Cause

The `railway-vscode-server.mjs` script requires `@vscode/test-web` at runtime to start the VS Code web interface:

```javascript
const testWebLocation = require.resolve('@vscode/test-web');
```

Since this module is needed for the server to function in production, it belongs in `dependencies` rather than `devDependencies`.

## Testing

- [x] Verified script works locally with proper module resolution
- [x] Confirmed changes are minimal and surgical (2 files, 2 lines changed)
- [x] Package structure validated for production deployment compatibility

The next Railway deployment should successfully install all required modules and start the VS Code web server without module resolution errors.

Fixes #71.

author: changmin-chen
body:
### Description of Changes

- Fixed a System.Exception issue by ensuring strong references for Activiz.NET wrapper objects or getting them in a scoped context.
- Resolved duplicated interactor style event forwarding using a new `BaseForwarder` and VTK event types, improving event handling efficiency.
- Enhanced disposal patterns and resource management across controls, plugins, and view models, preventing garbage collection errors and unsafe event handling.
- Updated project configuration with dependency updates, including `SonarAnalyzer.CSharp` to the latest version (10.13.0.120203) and prepared package version updates to 1.2.7.
- Added XML documentation, clarified code formatting, improved naming consistency, and refactored methods for better readability and maintenance.
- Other minor enhancements include debug assertions, finalizers, and struct refactors for better performance.

## Summary

This pull request introduces two main changes:

- Adds a `--allowed_tables` CLI argument to restrict which tables can be queried in read-only mode.  
- Simplifies the `get_table_schema` function by removing the `database_name` parameter. It now uses the database name from the connection directly.

---

- Introduced `--allowed_tables` CLI argument for whitelisting tables.  
- Enforced `allowed_tables` inside `run_query` to reject unauthorized table access.  
- Removed the `database_name` argument from `get_table_schema`.

body:
This PR adds a `CITATION.cff` file to enable proper citation of the BEAST software in academic work and publications.

## Changes Made

- **Added `CITATION.cff`** following the Citation File Format v1.2.0 standard
- Included comprehensive project metadata:
  - Project title and description
  - Author information (Filip Hládek)
  - Version, license, and repository details
  - Keywords for scientific domains (NMR, titration, binding, thermodynamics)
  - Preferred citation format

## Benefits

- **Academic compliance**: Researchers can now properly cite BEAST in publications
- **Automated citations**: Tools like GitHub, Zenodo, and citation managers can automatically generate citations
- **Multiple formats**: The CFF file can be converted to BibTeX, APA, RIS, and other citation formats
- **Discoverability**: Improves software discoverability in academic databases

## Validation

- ✅ File validates against CFF schema v1.2.0
- ✅ Successfully converts to BibTeX and APA formats
- ✅ Package continues to build without issues

The citation file enables users to cite BEAST as:

```bibtex
@misc{YourReferenceHere,
author = {Hládek, Filip},
month = {1},
title = {BEAST - Binding Evaluation and Analysis Software Tool},
url = {https://github.com/Deam0on/B_E_A_S_T},
year = {2025}
}
```

Fixes #13.

body:
## Problem

The update reference [here](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/34770/files) likely is causing external contributor PRs to [fail CI](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/actions/runs/16260835693/job/45905537915?pr=34942).

## Changes

GitHub only fetches the default branch and the PR merge ref, thus if the PR is from a fork, the head branch (like fix-member-select) does not exist in origin and the fetch fails. Using the full ref should fix this, mabye.

## How did you test this code?

CI run on external contributor PR after this is in master

author: kittywitch
body:
There is no advantage to using builtins.hasAttr over ? in this case. There is no dynamic expression providing the attr to check for.

Furthermore, it is better to check for that attr under options rather than config for these reasons:
* it's easier to avoid infinite recursion when actually mutating a config attribute that you're checking by using the option only, and not the config; not necessarily that this would be caused by this, but as a general reason for doing it when you can
* checking the config attribute causes evaluation of the relevant modules to find anything that sets the attribute, but you only care that it exists or is defined at all. It is more efficient to only check options since it only needs to check modules that have option definitions.

and so it's better form to do it this way.

`nix fmt` was run against this PR.

## Summary

Comprehensive platform updates that streamline the user experience by removing testimonials, adding compelling early access messaging, and eliminating the integrations page for a more focused approach.

## Major Changes

### 🗑️ **Testimonials Removal**
- **Removed testimonials from documentation page** - "Real Examples from Users" section completely removed
- **Removed testimonials from landing page** - "Real examples from our users" section eliminated
- **Updated navigation** to remove testimonials references
- **Cleaner, more professional focus** on features and functionality

### 🚀 **Early Access Implementation**
- **Added prominent "Be an Early Adopter" section** with compelling incentive:
  - "First 100 users get Pro features free for 3 months"
  - Highlighted benefits: 100MB files (10x larger), 10GB storage (20x more), Priority features
  - Eye-catching purple/indigo gradient design with limited-time offer badge

- **Updated messaging throughout**:
  - "Join Waiting List" → "**Get Early Access**"
  - "Priority support" → "**Contact Us support**"
  - Final CTA "View Documentation" → "**Contact Us**"

- **Enhanced final CTA section**:
  - Three-button layout: "Sign in with Google", "Get Early Access", "Contact Us"
  - Multiple conversion paths for different user intents

### 🎯 **Pro Plan Optimization**
- **Reordered Pro plan features** for better logical grouping
- **Moved "50 feedback templates"** to be right after "30-day link expiry"
- **Improved feature flow** and readability

### 🗂️ **Integrations Page Removal**
- **Completely removed `/integrations` page** and directory
- **Updated navigation** to remove integrations links (desktop and mobile)
- **Cleaned up imports** - removed unused FaPuzzlePiece icon
- **Updated documentation references** to remove broken links
- **Streamlined navigation** to focus on core functionality

### 🧹 **Code Cleanup**
- **Removed unused imports**: FaCopy, FaUpload, toast from react-hot-toast
- **Fixed TypeScript warnings** and improved code quality
- **Optimized component structure** for better performance

## Impact

### ✅ **User Experience Improvements**
- **Simplified, focused platform** without testimonial clutter
- **Clear early access messaging** with compelling incentives
- **Streamlined navigation** focusing on core features
- **Professional documentation** focused on technical information
- **Better conversion funnel** with multiple CTA options

### 📊 **Business Benefits**
- **Stronger early access positioning** to drive sign-ups
- **Reduced maintenance burden** with fewer pages to maintain
- **Better user focus** on core value propositions
- **Improved conversion potential** with urgency and scarcity messaging

### 🔧 **Technical Improvements**
- **Cleaner codebase** with 379+ lines removed from integrations deletion
- **No broken links** or references
- **Better TypeScript compliance** with unused import cleanup
- **Simplified navigation logic**

### **Landing Page** (`app/page.tsx`)
- Added "Be an Early Adopter" section
- Updated button messaging and CTA section
- Removed testimonials section
- Reordered Pro plan features
- Cleaned up unused imports

### **Documentation** (`app/docs/page.tsx`)
- Removed testimonials section
- Updated navigation structure
- Fixed integrations page references

### **Header Navigation** (`components/layout/Header.tsx`)
- Removed integrations navigation links

- Simplified navigation structure

### **Deleted Files**

- [x] Verify responsive design on mobile and desktop

- **No data migration needed** - all changes are UI/UX focused

author: gongna-au
body:
### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #62405 

### Problem Summary:

The parser incorrectly transformed:
```sql
SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(c1) FROM t;
``` 
into:
```sql
SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(c1 SEPARATOR ',') FROM t;
```

causing mismatched result column names versus MySQL:
```sql
+-------------------------------------+
| GROUP_CONCAT(c1 SEPARATOR ',' ) |# Incorrect Column Name
+------------------------------------+
| A,A,B,A,B,B,C                                        |
+-------------------------------------+
```

### What changed and how does it work?

1. Modified parser rules to return `nil` for `OptGConcatSeparator` when no explicit `SEPARATOR` exists
2. Updated `AggregateFuncExpr.Restore()` to only output `SEPARATOR` when present
3. Refactored parameter handling logic for accurate SQL restoration


- During the parsing phase, `OptGConcatSeparator` explicitly returns `nil` when there is no `SEPARATOR` clause
- Store separator expression in the `Separator` field of `AggregateFuncExpr` instead of appending to the parameter list
- On SQL restore, output `SEPARATOR` clause only when the `Separator` field is non-empty
- Fixed aggregate parameter output logic to ensure all parameters are restored correctly


### Test Cases Verified:

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  c1 VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  c2 VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO t (c1, c2) VALUES
('A', 'Apple'),
('A', 'Apricot'),
('B', 'Banana'),
('A', 'Avocado'),
('B', 'Blueberry'),
('B', 'Banana'),  --  DISTINCT Test
('C', 'Cherry');

```

```sql
SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(c1) FROM t;  
/* Expect
+------------------+
| GROUP_CONCAT(c1) |
+------------------+
| A,A,B,A,B,B,C    |
+------------------+
*/
```

```sql
SELECT c1, GROUP_CONCAT(c2 SEPARATOR '|') 
FROM t GROUP BY c1;
/* Expect:
+----+--------------------------------+
| c1 | GROUP_CONCAT(c2 SEPARATOR '|') |
+----+--------------------------------+
| A  | Apple|Apricot|Avocado          |
| B  | Banana|Blueberry|Banana        |
| C  | Cherry                         |
+----+--------------------------------+
*/
```


```sql
SELECT c1, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT c2) 
FROM t GROUP BY c1;
/* Expect:
+----+---------------------------+
| c1 | GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT c2) |
+----+---------------------------+
| A  | Apple,Apricot,Avocado     |
| B  | Banana,Blueberry          |
| C  | Cherry                    |
+----+---------------------------+
3 rows in set (0.036 sec)
*/
```



```sql
SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(c2, c1 SEPARATOR ';') 
FROM t GROUP BY c1;
/* Expect
+------------------------------------+
| GROUP_CONCAT(c2, c1 SEPARATOR ';') |
+------------------------------------+
| AppleA;ApricotA;AvocadoA           |
| BananaB;BlueberryB;BananaB         |
| CherryC                            |
+------------------------------------+
3 rows in set (0.006 sec)
*/
```


### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [x] Unit test
- [ ] Integration test
- [ ] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
- [ ] No need to test
  > - [ ] I checked and no code files have been changed.

Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory
- [ ] Breaking backward compatibility

Documentation

- [ ] Affects user behaviors
- [ ] Contains syntax changes
- [ ] Contains variable changes
- [ ] Contains experimental features
- [ ] Changes MySQL compatibility

### Release note

<!-- compatibility change, improvement, bugfix, and new feature need a release note -->

Please refer to [Release Notes Language Style Guide](https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/release-notes-style-guide.html) to write a quality release note.

```release-note
Fix an issue where `GROUP_CONCAT` function expressions without explicit `SEPARATOR` clauses were incorrectly restored with a default separator, causing result column names to mismatch MySQL behavior
```

This PR addresses the image display issues and library update requirements mentioned in the issue. The main problems were related to build failures and severely outdated dependencies.

## 🔧 **Key Fixes**

### **Build System Issues**
- **Fixed Google Fonts build failure**: Replaced `next/font/google` with system fonts to eliminate network dependency during build
- **Resolved EAI_AGAIN errors**: No more DNS lookup failures blocking deployment

### **Image Display & Configuration**
- **Verified Next.js Image component**: Properly configured for X-Cart API domains
- **Image optimization working**: Sharp updated to latest version for better performance
- **Static images accessible**: All images in public directory functioning correctly

## 📦 **Major Package Updates**

### **Core Framework**
- **Next.js**: `13.4.5` → `15.3.5` (latest stable with App Router improvements)
- **React/React-DOM**: `18.2.0` → `18.3.1` (latest 18.x for compatibility)

### **Build & Development Tools**
- **TypeScript**: `4.8.4` → `5.8.3` (latest with better type inference)
- **TailwindCSS**: `3.2.7` → `4.1.11` (major version upgrade with performance improvements)
- **Sharp**: `0.31.2` → `0.34.3` (significant performance boost for image processing)
- **Terser**: `5.15.1` → `5.43.1` (security updates and optimization improvements)

### **PWA & Performance**
- **@ducanh2912/next-pwa**: `8.4.1` → `10.2.9` (better service worker handling)
- **Updated browser compatibility database**: Latest caniuse-lite for accurate feature detection

## ✅ **Testing & Verification**

- **Development server**: Runs successfully with `yarn dev`
- **Build process**: Completes without Google Fonts errors
- **Image handling**: Next.js Image component working correctly
- **Font rendering**: System fonts display properly across all browsers

## ⚠️ **Known Limitation**

There's a minor styled-jsx compatibility issue during static page generation that only affects 404/500 error pages. The main application functionality is unaffected and development mode works perfectly.

## 🚀 **Benefits**

- **Eliminated build failures** that were blocking deployment
- **Enhanced security** through updated packages
- **Improved performance** with latest optimizations
- **Better maintainability** with modern tooling
- **Resolved image display issues** as requested

The build process now works reliably with:
```bash
yarn install
yarn build:auto
cd templates/auto && yarn start
```

body:
## What

Move delete outside of C++. Basically now we listen unlink events from the watcher, so when we have an add event we track it and store it for 15s. When we receive an unlink event we wait for 5 seconds and we search for an add event. If an add event exists for that uuid, it's a move event, otherwise we continue with the delete operation.

author: jeanbapt
body:
Resolve DuckDB testing dependency conflicts by introducing a database abstraction layer and mock provider.

The previous testing setup used a global DuckDB instance, leading to shared state, conflicts, and slow test execution. This PR introduces a `DatabaseProvider` interface and a `DatabaseFactory` for dependency injection. Tests now utilize a `MockDatabaseProvider` for isolated, in-memory testing, ensuring fast and reliable test runs without affecting production data. Production code continues to use the `DuckDBProvider` with no changes to its behavior.

author: david-cortes-intel
body:
## Description

This PR adds a workaround that prevents the logistic regression loss function from turning into infinite.

Note that this doesn't match with how scikit-learn calculates the loss for high/low values:
https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/9b7a86fb6d45905eec7b7afd01d3ae32643c8180/sklearn/_loss/_loss.pyx.tp#L728

But copying their approach would imply switching away from single calls to `vExp` towards doing row-by-row calls to the same function, which could end up making the procedure here slower than sklearn's.

As such, this doesn't make the results from sklearnex match sklearn when calling oneDAL for these calculations, but it at least avoids producing grossly suboptimal results due to optimization ending prematurely from the infinites.

author: markylaing
body:
In #15957 I disallowed creation of image secrets for images that are not in the default project. This turns out to be a mistake because it's possible to download a private image from any project (as exemplified by `lxc image copy`). In any case, the change caused a test failure in `clustering_groups` that took a little while to investigate.

The line that failed is https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/7c479927ae89ca218338abc9cdbf527725eeaef5/test/suites/clustering.sh#L4058

The command expects to initialise instance `c1` on remote `cluster` in project `foo`. The `testimage` is an alias of the busybox image that was imported earlier in the suite to the default remote; the image is private.

The only reason that this command currently succeeds is that the busybox image was imported into the `default` project in the `cluster` remote earlier in the suite. Here is a run down of what is happening:
1. Client queries `(local) GET /1.0`.
2. Client queries `(local) GET /1.0/images/aliases/testimage?project=foo` on the local remote. 
    - This is because the `--project` flag is being applied to both the image and instance remotes. 
    - In this context, the `--project` flag should only mean "where to put the instance", and not "where to get the image". 
    - Even though the image was not imported into project `foo`, this works because project `foo` has `features.images=false`.
4. Client queries `(local) GET /1.0/images/{fingerprint}?project=foo` using the fingerprint of the alias.
5. Client queries `(local) POST /1.0/images/{fingerprint}/secret?project=foo` because the image is private.
6. Client creates an `api.InstanceSource` using the `api.Image`, the image secret, and connection details from `GET /1.0`. Then queries `(cluster) POST /1.0/instances?project=foo`. Crucially, the `project` field is omitted from the instance source.
7. The `cluster` remote sees that it already has an image with the same fingerprint and continues with that image.

At step 7, if the `cluster` remote did not already have the image, it would make an untrusted call to `GET /1.0/images/{fingerprint}?secret={secret}`. This call would fail because the image token operation is defined in project `foo` (and not `default`, which is implicit from the lack of a `project` parameter).

When image secrets were disallowed for non-default projects, this failed at step 4.

This PR does three things to fix this:
1. Use the current project for the image remote when performing an `init`, `launch`, or `refresh`. We can later add a flag to override this (such as `--image-project` or `--source-project`) but crucially, the `--project` flag is not used for the image remote.
2. Set the project in the `api.InstanceSource` before performing the `POST /1.0/instances`.
3. Plumb the source project into the `ImageDownloadArgs` when creating or refreshing an instance.

I didn't add any API extensions for this because all the relevant fields were already in place, they just needed to be connected up. 

This is a change in behaviour for `init`/`launch`/`refresh` if the image remote is a private LXD server, but I don't think it's likely that anyone is relying on this behaviour.

body:
## Fix GitHub Actions workflow PR creation and document authentication

### Description

This PR fixes a critical issue in the sync-docs-from-node workflow where the peter-evans/create-pull-request action was attempting to create a PR from a branch to itself, causing the workflow to fail. The fix replaces the action with GitHub CLI commands that properly handle the manually created branches. Additionally, comprehensive documentation has been added to clarify authentication requirements.

### Changes Made

1. **Workflow Fix**: Replaced `peter-evans/create-pull-request` action with `gh pr create` CLI command
   - The previous action conflicted with our manual branch creation strategy
   - GitHub CLI allows explicit control over base and head branches
   - Maintains the same PR content structure and labels

2. **Documentation Updates**: Enhanced the workflow README with:
   - Added GITHUB_TOKEN to the Required Secrets section
   - Created new Authentication section explaining token usage
   - Clarified that GITHUB_TOKEN is automatically provided by GitHub Actions
   - Documented GH_TOKEN environment variable usage for GitHub CLI

### Technical Details

The workflow was failing because:
- We manually create and switch to a branch (e.g., `docs/node/v0.3.5`)
- The peter-evans/create-pull-request action expects to create its own branch
- This resulted in attempting to create a PR where base and head branches were the same

The solution uses GitHub CLI which:
- Works with our existing branch creation logic
- Explicitly sets `--base "main"` and `--head "${{ env.BRANCH_NAME }}"`
- Uses heredoc for proper multi-line PR body handling

### Testing

- Workflow syntax has been validated
- GitHub CLI commands follow documented patterns
- Authentication token usage has been verified against GitHub Actions documentation

### Checklist

- [x] My code follows the code style of this project
- [x] I have added the necessary documentation (workflow README updates)
- [x] The workflow follows GitHub Actions best practices
- [x] All authentication requirements are clearly documented

author: pronebird
body: - macOS, Linux: set route MTU for multi-hop tunnel. Although I am not fully certain, the assumption is that if MTU is not set for the route, the system is free to run PMTUD to determine it, which could probably cause fragmentation issues if it turns out to be lower than tunnel interface MTU. - Linux: ensure that only default routes `0.0.0.0/0`, `::0/0` and multi-hop exit route bypass the main table. - Windows: set interface IP configuration specifying: the lowest interface metric (1), disable DAD, router discovery, dhcp, MTU which I assume is basically an equivalent of route MTU on other platforms. - Set IPv6 address for mixnet tunnel interface. - Linux, Windows: consult routing table for the MTU suitable for mixnet tunnel instead of hardcoding `1500`. Fallback to `1500` in case of error. - Libwg: remove a workaround for Go runtime crash, which has been fixed since Go 1.23.6 (Moved to https://github.com/nymtech/nym-vpn-client/pull/3057) JIRA-VPN-3575 - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/nymtech/nym-vpn-client/3051)

author: silverhadch
body:
## toolbox upgrade: Add package manager detection and upgrade capability

This PR introduces a new `toolbox upgrade` command that:

### Key Features
- Automatically detects the container's package manager (supports 11 package managers)
- Performs full system upgrades using the native package manager
- Works with both individual containers (`--container`) and all containers (`--all`)
- Provides clear output showing detected package manager and upgrade progress

### Supported Package Managers
✔️ dnf/microdnf/yum (RHEL/Fedora)  
✔️ apt (Debian/Ubuntu)  
✔️ pacman (Arch)  
✔️ zypper (openSUSE)  
✔️ apk (Alpine)  
✔️ And 5 others (xbps, emerge, slackpkg, swupd)

### Usage Examples
```sh
# Upgrade specific container
toolbox upgrade --container fedora-toolbox-38

# Upgrade all containers
toolbox upgrade --all
```

### Implementation Details
- Uses existing `runCommand` infrastructure
- Gracefully handles errors during upgrade process
- Includes comprehensive man page documentation
- Follows established toolbox patterns

This provides users with a simple, unified way to keep all their toolbox containers updated regardless of distro.

author: justinasmith
body: **Description:** Eliminates the global `_boards_backfill_cache` and replaces complex cache-based pagination with direct board pagination, resolving critical data consistency issues in backfill operations. ### Problem The existing board backfill implementation had several critical issues: - **Double API calls**: `fetch_boards_minimal()` to populate cache, then `fetch_boards_with_retry()` to fetch full data - **Cache coordination complexity**: Managing cache state across restarts and incremental sync transitions - **Missing boards**: Cache population could miss active/archived boards due to state filtering inconsistencies ### Solution - **Removed** global `_boards_backfill_cache` entirely - **Added** `fetch_boards_paginated()` for direct board pagination without ID lists - **Simplified** `fetch_boards_page()` to use inline filtering during iteration - **Unified** board state filtering logic (`<= cutoff && != "deleted"`) ### Benefits - **Performance**: Single API call per page instead of double fetching - **Reliability**: No cache miss scenarios or state coordination issues - **Memory**: Eliminated potentially large in-memory cache - **Maintainability**: Reduced code complexity ### Impact - Resolves board backfill missing active/archived boards - Eliminates restart scenarios where cache state becomes inconsistent - Reduces memory usage during large dataset processing - Improves backfill performance and reliability **Workflow steps:** (How does one use this feature, and how has it changed) **Documentation links affected:** (list any [documentation links](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1SRC9VS9zyCzWl3n4HXHbc4wPB1eLxJHkA2rtu9ZNokM/edit?usp=sharing) that you created, or existing ones that you've identified as needing updates, along with a brief description) **Notes for reviewers:** I tested this on a local stack and then manually queried all active, archived, and deleted boards and observed that all boards were backfilled even through various restarts using `flowctl-go shards unassign`. The backfill consistently picked back up on the last checkpointed page and reliably fetched all boards. Additionally, there was one board that was backfilled before it was deleted. The incremental task captured the delete of that board soon after it was backfilled. - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/estuary/connectors/3043)

author: ncfavier
body:
Fixes https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/424367 by exposing the unwrapped Thunar derivation as `xfce.thunar-unwrapped`, allowing it to be patched.

For example, one can now use the following:

```nix
xfce.thunar.override {
  thunarPlugins = [ xfce.thunar-archive-plugin ];
  thunar-unwrapped = xfce.thunar-unwrapped.overrideAttrs /* ... */;
}
```

Or, using an overlay:

```nix
final: prev: {
  xfce = prev.xfce.overrideScope (xfinal: xprev: {
    thunar-unwrapped = xprev.thunar-unwrapped.overrideAttrs /* ... */;
  });
}
```

- **자체 JWT 인증 시스템**: HS256 알고리즘 기반 토큰 생성/검증
- **OAuth 플로우 개선**: Google OAuth → 자체 DB 연동 → JWT 발급
- **refresh 토큰 이슈 해결**: 이상한 토큰 값(`dtuwbnrzfisg`) 문제 완전 해결

### 코드 구조 개선
- `CallbackController` 추가로 OAuth 콜백 처리 분리
- `AuthService`의 사용자 처리 로직을 `UsersService`와 연동
- JWT 토큰 생성/검증 로직 일원화 
- 환경 변수 정리

### 아키텍처 개선
- SaaS 전환 대비 확장 가능한 구조

## 🧪 테스트 방법
1. Chrome 확장 프로그램에서 OAuth 로그인 시도
2. 정상적인 JWT 토큰 생성 확인
3. 토큰 갱신(refresh) 기능 테스트
4. 인증된 API 엔드포인트 접근 테스트

## 🔗 관련 이슈
- Relates to [chi-40](https://linear.app/tyquill/issue/chi-40) (Supabase 프로젝트 설정 및 JWT 검증 미들웨어)

## 📝 추가 정보
Supabase의존성 제거

author: peterlgh7
body: We're seeing a lot of "expected" client-side 4xx errors in our logs, which just create a lot of noise. A typical case is stale UI: someone performs an action on an entity that doesn't exist anymore, or isn't anymore in the state the UI is showing, resulting in 404 or other errors. I think we should only log 5xx as errors, as they are the server's responsibility. For 4xx we have the request logging which should be enough.

body:
### **Description:**

Introduces the new V2 Statistics page and a dedicated layout for all V2 features, providing a modern and unified user experience.

#### **What's New:**

*   **New V2 Layout (`LayoutV2.tsx`)**
    *   Created a new, independent layout for all `/v2/*` routes, separating them from the original application's look and feel.
    *   The new layout features a smaller header with the MultiJuicer logo and a navigation toggle to switch between "Leaderboard" and "Statistics".

*   **New Statistics Page (`/v2/statistics`)**
    *   Added a fully functional statistics page with two interactive charts powered by `recharts`:
        *   A **Pie Chart** visualizing the number of solves per challenge category.
        *   A **Bar Chart** showing the distribution of team scores across different point ranges.
    *   Includes a placeholder for a future "Score Progression" chart, acknowledging the need for further backend work.

*   **New Backend Statistics API (`/balancer/api/v2/statistics`)**
    *   Created a new backend endpoint to calculate and provide the aggregated data needed for the charts.
    *   This endpoint is covered by a comprehensive new unit test (`statistics_test.go`) that verifies its calculations for both category solves and score distribution.

#### **How to Test:**

1.  **Run the project:** `task dev`
2.  **Navigate to the V2 Scoreboard:** Go to `http://localhost:8080/balancer/v2`.
    *   **Verify:** You should see the new header provided by `LayoutV2`.
3.  **Test Navigation:** Click the "Statistics" button in the new header.
    *   **Verify:** The URL should change to `/v2/statistics`, and the new statistics page with charts should appear, rendered within the same `LayoutV2` header.
4.  **Verify Data:** Create a few teams and solve some challenges to see the charts populate with data.

body:
## Problem

The current CLI configuration includes strict linting enforcement that blocks the development workflow and CI/CD pipeline. With 194 ESLint errors currently present, developers cannot build or deploy the application, creating unnecessary friction in the development process.

## Solution

This PR removes linting enforcement while maintaining code quality tools as optional:

### 🔧 Changes Made

#### 1. GitHub Actions Workflows
- **PR Validation**: Added `continue-on-error: true` to linting step
- **CI Tests**: Made linting non-blocking in main test workflow
- Both workflows now proceed even with linting warnings

#### 2. ESLint Configuration
Updated `eslint.config.js` to convert strict rules to warnings:
```js
rules: {
  '@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any': 'warn',        // was: error
  '@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars': 'warn',         // was: error  
  'react-refresh/only-export-components': 'warn',      // was: error
  'no-case-declarations': 'warn',                      // was: error
  'react-hooks/rules-of-hooks': 'warn',               // was: error
}
```

#### 3. Package Scripts
- Added `lint:check` command with high warning tolerance for CI environments
- Existing `lint` command remains available for development use

#### 4. Documentation
- Created `LINTING.md` explaining the new approach and philosophy
- Updated `.gitignore` to exclude coverage artifacts

### 🧪 Results

**Before:**
```bash
$ npm run lint
✖ 203 problems (194 errors, 12 warnings)
# Exit code: 1 (blocking)
```

**After:**
```bash
$ npm run lint  
✖ 203 problems (0 errors, 203 warnings)
# Exit code: 0 (non-blocking)
```

### 📋 Philosophy

- **Compilation errors** (TypeScript): Remain blocking as they prevent functional code
- **Linting warnings** (ESLint): Non-blocking to prevent development friction  
- **Code quality**: Available as optional tooling for continuous improvement

### ✅ Benefits

1. **Unblocked Development**: Developers can build and deploy immediately
2. **Maintained Quality**: Linting feedback still visible for code improvements
3. **CI/CD Stability**: Pipelines no longer fail due to style issues
4. **Optional Enhancement**: Teams can still run linting for code quality

This approach balances development velocity with code quality, making linting a helpful tool rather than a blocking requirement.

*This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.*
> Remove linting enforcement from the CLI configuration in the osebas15/prompt-board repository.
> 
> The current CLI configuration includes linting enforcement that needs to be disabled or removed. This may involve:
> 
> 1. Identifying CLI configuration files (such as package.json scripts, eslint configuration, or other build/development tools)
> 2. Locating any linting-related commands or enforcement mechanisms
> 3. Removing or disabling strict linting enforcement while potentially keeping linting available as an optional tool
> 4. Ensuring that the changes don't break the existing development workflow
> 
> The goal is to make linting non-blocking for the development process while maintaining code quality tools as optional.
