author: lucaseck
body:
Fixes: #69 

### What was the problem/requirement? (What/Why)
We have sample recipes for many DCCs, but not Houdini yet.

### What was the solution? (How)
This PR builds on the work done in #76 to clean up a few things and get it merge ready since that PR seems to have stalled out. Thank you to @dzavada for the initial request and work to get a Houdini sample included. Main changes from #76:
* Removal of the use of LD_LIBRARY_PATH and instead add rpaths to $ORIGIN to any of the system libraries brought in by doing a dnf install
  * This was based on reading https://rattler.build/v0.35.6/internals/#making-packages-relocatable-with-rattler-build which notes that rpaths are added to $ORIGIN by rattler-build. When checking the dsolib folder in an extracted package I was seeing that most .so libraries had $ORIGIN as an rpath except for any that were copied over from the dnf downloads. 
* Swapped the build from conda-build to rattler-build which brought build times down from ~35min to ~7-8 minutes
* Removed some additional libraries from the dnf install command since they don't appear to be required for headless rendering
* Removed any setting of SESI_LMHOST from being in the package itself. This should be done as either a queue env or some other setup action not belonging to the package
* Added a sourceDownloadInstructions line
* I've also added a small README 

### What is the impact of this change?
Customers can build their Houdini Conda packages and configure them as desired. e.g. adding SideFXLabs into the package, changing to new versions, adding new system libraries.

### How was this change tested?

- Built the new package following the instructions in this package for setting up a build farm on Deadline Cloud and then did a submission `./submit-package-job houdini-20.5`. I verified that the package built and the tests passed.
- I did a real render using the package I built and the adaptor package from the deadline-cloud channel and verified the render succeeded, the output looked correct, and that my package was the one used.

### Was this change documented?
A small README is included

body:
## [0.1.7]

### Description

We are migrating the managed EC2 AWS Batch Compute Environments to Fargate to prevent the need for AMI updates and to hopefully resolve the issue we are seeing with the ECS agent on EC2 instances.

Issues:

- https://github.com/podaac/generate/issues/25
- https://jira.jpl.nasa.gov/browse/PODAAC-6941

Documentation on issue:

- https://wiki.jpl.nasa.gov/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=826914206#GenerateCloudFailures&Recovery-2025-07-05-2025-07-07P&Sfailures


### Overview of work done

- Generate: Adds Fargate compute resources for batch jobs
- Generate: Removes lifeycle 'create_before_destroy' for EC2 compute resources since this policy was preventing terraform from applying the changes
- P&S: Added source hash in terraform file so it can detect changes to the job config json file
- P&S: Set retires to 0 so it only runs once
- Downloader, Combiner, Processor, Uploader, License Returner: Updated job definition/resources for Fargate instead of EC2
- Error Handler: Update EventBridge rule to ignore P&S failures.


### Overview of verification done

- Tested in SIT on three OBPG L2 granules for MODIS Aqua to produce two L2P granules

### Overview of integration done

- Tested in UAT on 7/16/2025 - 7/17/2025 time range
- Analysis of results is located here: https://wiki.jpl.nasa.gov/display/PD/Generate+-+Cloud+-+UAT+Test+v0.1.7#GenerateCloudUATTestv0.1.7-RESULTS

### Test Summary

UAT JOB METRICS:

- Total Cost: ~$157.26
- Average Execution Time: 9.65 minutes
- Average Number of Granules: 33

OPS JOB METRICS:

- Total Cost: ~$237.41 (May include other services)
- Average Execution Time: 8.8 minutes
- Average Number of Granules: 37

NOTES:

- The main difference we saw between UAT and OPS is OPS is operating in a degraded state which requires occasional manual intervention. UAT seems to have produce the usual amount of files without errors and therefore producing more granules that OPS. 
- We did see a difference in the number and average execution time of granules between UAT and OPS. This could be due to the Fargate platform which has typically had slightly longer execution times than EC2. Despite this, it seems that Generate will execute hourly on Fargate and still produce the same number of granules.

author: oswcab
body:
As described in the issue in the reference down below, the creation of a custom worker pool fails when there is no 'additional_security_group_ids' specified, when it points to an empty list or when the list contains only an empty string (as in the examples in this repository).

The Red Hat's terraform-provider-rhcs provider [1] defines this attribute as optional:

    "additional_security_group_ids": {
        "type": [
          "list",
          "string"
        ],
        "description": "Additional security group ids. After the creation of the resource, it is not possible to update the attribute value.",
        "description_kind": "plain",
        "optional": true
      }

This commit changes the 'aws_node_pool' variable to reflect the optional nature of this attribute; after applying this change, the custom pool creation is successful.

[1] https://github.com/terraform-redhat/terraform-provider-rhcs

Fixes #78

author: datagen24
body:
# Elasticsearch Compatibility Mode: `compatibility_mode` Option

## Motivation
Some deployments use Elasticsearch server v8.x, but the Python client library may be v9.x. By default, the v9 client sends Accept headers with `compatible-with=9`, which are not accepted by ES 8.x servers. This causes errors unless the client is forced to use compatibility mode.

## Summary of Changes
- **Config Option:** Added `compatibility_mode` to the `elasticsearch` section of `mcp_config.yaml` (documented, not committed).
- **Client Update:** The `ElasticsearchClient` now reads this option and, if enabled, passes `compatibility_mode=True` to the Python Elasticsearch client.
- **Documentation:**
  - Updated `docs/README.md` with configuration and usage instructions.
  - Updated `docs/Implementation_Docs/ENHANCED_THREAT_INTELLIGENCE_IMPLEMENTATION.md` with motivation, implementation details, and impact.

## Configuration Example
```yaml
elasticsearch:
  url: "https://your-es-server:9200"
  username: "..."
  password: "..."
  verify_ssl: true
  compatibility_mode: true
  # ... other options ...
```

- Set `compatibility_mode: true` if you see errors about Accept headers or are running an ES 8.x server with a v9.x Python client.
- Leave as `false` if your client and server are the same major version or you do not need compatibility headers.

## Impact
- Resolves compatibility issues between ES v9 Python client and ES v8 server.
- No impact on existing deployments unless the option is enabled.

---
Closes #51

## Overview
This PR introduces a comprehensive blockchain-based estate planning system built on Stacks using Clarity smart contracts. The system provides decentralized, transparent, and secure estate planning services through five interconnected contracts.

## Changes Made

### New Contracts Added
1. **will-preparation.clar** - Manages legal document creation and witness requirements
2. **trust-administration.clar** - Handles complex estate planning and asset protection
3. **beneficiary-coordination.clar** - Ensures proper inheritance distribution and documentation
4. **tax-planning.clar** - Minimizes estate tax obligations and maximizes inheritance value
5. **executor-support.clar** - Assists designated individuals with estate administration duties

### Key Features Implemented

#### Will Preparation Contract
- ✅ Will creation with witness requirements (minimum 2 witnesses)
- ✅ Digital signature collection from witnesses
- ✅ Will revocation and content updates
- ✅ Comprehensive witness validation system
- ✅ Testator authorization controls

#### Trust Administration Contract
- ✅ Trust creation with grantor, trustee, and beneficiary roles
- ✅ Asset management and distribution tracking
- ✅ Beneficiary allocation with percentage-based distributions
- ✅ Conditional distribution logic
- ✅ Trust termination capabilities

#### Beneficiary Coordination Contract
- ✅ Beneficiary registration and verification system

#### Tax Planning Contract
- ✅ Federal estate tax calculations (2023 rates and exemptions)

#### Executor Support Contract
- ✅ Estate creation and probate process management
- ✅ Task assignment and completion tracking
- ✅ Document upload and verification system
- ✅ Compensation calculation and hour tracking
- ✅ Probate milestone management

### Technical Implementation

#### Data Structures
- Comprehensive maps for storing estate, trust, beneficiary, and tax data
- Efficient counter systems for unique ID generation
- Optional types for flexible data handling
- Proper data validation and constraints

#### Access Control
- Role-based permissions (testator, executor, beneficiary, witness, trustee)
- Multi-signature support for critical operations
- Authorization checks on all sensitive functions
- Contract owner privileges for administrative tasks

#### Error Handling
- Comprehensive error codes for all failure scenarios
- Descriptive error messages for debugging
- Input validation on all public functions
- Proper assertion checks throughout

#### Security Features
- Principal-based authentication
- Immutable audit trails
- Witness requirement enforcement

- Integration testing scenarios
- Mock data for realistic testing

### Configuration Files

- ✅ Native Clarity syntax (no HTML entities)
- ✅ Proper comparison operators (\`<\`, \`>\`, \`<=\`, \`>=\`)
- ✅ Consistent naming conventions (kebab-case)

- Efficient data structures

- Modular contract design

   \`\`\`bash
   # Install Clarinet CLI

## Usage Examples

### Creating a Will
\`\`\`clarity
(contract-call? .will-preparation create-will

## Previously
### https://github.com/DevExpress/DevExtreme/pull/30092

## Failed test (only Vue)
https://github.com/DevExpress/DevExtreme/actions/runs/16262938881?pr=30351 
https://github.com/DevExpress/DevExtreme/actions/runs/16262938881/job/45917687197?pr=30351

## Thoughts
Presumably due to the asynchronous mechanism of calling the update() hook. VUE.nextTick() emulation is possible required. The issue may be related to animation.

## Reason
In Vue, due to the nextTick() mechanism, the Toolbar is rendered from the microtask queue (since nextTick is a Promise.then callback: https://github.com/vuejs/core/blob/main/packages/runtime-core/src/scheduler.ts#L50). This happens after all resize events have been triggered, but it should happen before.

I removed the previous resize event call and tied this call to the moment between renderVisibility and animateShowing. This also allowed me to remove unnecessary calls to this event.

author: cwmiller1
body:
# Contributing to CSrankings

Thanks for contributing to CSrankings! Please read and indicate you agree with **all** these guidelines to getting your pull request accepted. Note that pull requests may take some time to get merged (please don't contact us for at least three months for updates, unless you are a sponsor - see below).

**If you find CSrankings useful, [please consider becoming a sponsor](https://github.com/sponsors/csrankings).**

**NOTE:** IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW THE STEPS BELOW, YOUR PULL REQUEST WILL BE SUMMARILY REJECTED.
You must read and check **all** the boxes below by filling them in with an X or your PR will be rejected.

**The Basics**

- [x] All pull requests and issues must come from non-anonymous accounts. Make sure your GitHub profile contains your full name.

- [x] Use a reasonable title that explains what the PR corresponds to (as in, not "Update csrankings-x.csv").

- [x] Combine multiple updates to a single institution into a **single PR.**

- [x] Only submit one pull request per institution.

- [x] Do not modify any files except `csrankings-[a-z].csv` or (if needed) `country-info.csv` and `old/industry.csv` (see below).

- [x] Do not use Excel to edit any .csv files; Excel incorrectly tries to
convert some Google Scholar entries to formulas, corrupting the
database. Use the GitHub user interface or a text editor like emacs or NotePad instead.

- [x] Insert new faculty **in alphabetical order** (not at the end) in the appropriate `csrankings-[a-z].csv` files. **Do not modify `csrankings.csv`, which is auto-generated.**

- [x] Check to make sure that you have no spaces after commas, or any missing fields.

- [x] Check to make sure the home page is correct.

- [x] Make sure the Google Scholar IDs are just the alphanumeric identifier (not a URL or with `&hl=en`).

- [x] Check to make sure the name corresponds to the DBLP entry (look it up at http://dblp.org).

- [x] If a faculty member is not in a CS department or similar, include a comment explaining how they meet the inclusion criteria (see below).

**Inclusion criteria**

- [x] Make sure that any faculty you add meet the inclusion
criteria. Eligible faculty include only full-time, tenure-track research
faculty members on a given campus who can *solely* advise PhD students in
Computer Science. Faculty not in a CS department or similar who can
advise PhD students in CS can be included regardless of their home
department. **Provide justification, pointing to specific home pages
showing how faculty not in a CS department meet the inclusion criteria,
e.g. showing a courtesy appointment in CS.** Faculty must also have a 75%+ time appointment (check
`old/industry.csv` for faculty who are now more than 25% in industry).

**Updating an affiliation or home page**

- [x] Update affiliations, home pages, and Google Scholar entries by modifying `csrankings-[a-z].csv`. For the Google Scholar entry, just use the alphanumeric identifier in the middle of the URL. If none is there, put `NOSCHOLARPAGE`.

**Adding one or more faculty members (including an entire department)**

- [x] If the department is not yet listed in CSrankings, the entire CS faculty needs to be added (not just one faculty member).

- [x] Enter each faculty member's [DBLP](http://dblp.org) name, home page, and Google Scholar entry (just the alphanumeric identifier, not the whole URL) by modifying `csrankings-[a-z].csv` (**the letters correspond to the first letter of the faculty members' names**); include disambiguation suffixes like `0001` as needed. If the faculty entry is currently ambiguous, please do not include them. Send mail to the DBLP maintainers (dblp@dagstuhl.de) with a few publications by a particular faculty member; also, open an issue so that when the DBLP database is updated, that faculty member's information can be added.

- [x] If DBLP has multiple entries for this person, *all of them need to be listed*. Do not update `dblp-aliases.csv`.

- [x] If the institution you are adding is not in the US,
update `country-info.csv` and add *all* of the faculty in the CS department.

**(Advanced) Quick contribution via a shallow clone** 

We recommend that you use the GitHub web user interface to make changes. However, it may be more convenient
to clone the repository for larger-scale changes.

However, a full clone of the CSrankings repository is almost 2GB.  To
contribute a change without creating a full local clone of the
CSrankings repo, you can perform a _shallow clone_.  To do so, follow these
steps:

1. Fork the CSrankings repo.  If you have an existing fork, but it is not up to date with the main repository, this technique may not work.  If necessary, delete and re-create your fork to get it up to date.  (Do **not** delete your existing fork if it has unmerged changes you want to preserve!)

1. Do a shallow clone of your fork: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/yourusername/CSrankings`.  This will only download the most recent commit, not the full git history.

1. Make your changes on a branch, push them to your clone, and create a pull request on GitHub as usual.

If you want to make another contribution and some time has passed, perform these steps again, creating a fresh fork and shallow clone.

body:
<!--
The Qwik Team and Community appreciate all PRs. Thank you for your effort! Not all PRs can be merged, but those that meet the following criteria will be prioritized:

a) Core fixes, and

b) Framework functionality achievable only by the core.

If this PR can be done as a 3rd-Party Community Add-On, we encourage that for quicker adoption.

If you believe your functionality is valuable to the entire Qwik Community, discuss it in the Qwik Discord channels for potential inclusion in the core.

First of all, make sure your PR title is descriptive and matches our commit title guidelines.

Also make sure your PR follows all the guidelines in the [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) document.

-->

# What is it?

<!-- pick one and remove the others -->

- Bug

# Description

`invalidateModule` is used for HMR in Vite `handleHotUpdate` hook. It was added in https://github.com/QwikDev/qwik/commit/a69de93ef5d2ebf1ae3a92c18879fafcb3d86cbd in an attempt to make sure that QRLs also get updated on parent changes.

The problem is that this causes cypress component tests (CCTs) to be 10x slower, eventually leading to CCTs startup timing out with a "Error: Code(5): You can render over a existing q:container. Skipping render()." message.

I tried many possible combinations of updating the child, the parent, the jsx, the useVisibleTask, the useTask, the QRL outside of the component... I haven't been able to trigger a case where the `invalidateModule` in the `transform` hook with the optimizer would ever run.

What seems to happen is that the `handleHotUpdate` hook will invalidate the module, which will then trigger the `transform` hook for the corresponding module and its QRLs.

Here's an example log:
```
invalidating module HMR /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx
invalidating module HMR /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx
invalidating module HMR /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx
invalidating module HMR /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx
transform /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx
transform /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx
transform /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx_Counter2_component_div_button_onClick_fDhgqdXxNQQ.js
transform /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx_Counter2_component_yQ6Hre9qSVo.js
transform /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx_Counter2_component_useVisibleTask_ISI2k8PkKII.js
transform /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx_Counter2_component_computedCount_useComputed_OKKHalBLW9E.js
transform /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx_Counter2_component_computedCount_useComputed_OKKHalBLW9E.js
transform /Users/maieul/dev/playgrounds/qwik-express/src/components/counter2.tsx_Counter2_component_useVisibleTask_ISI2k8PkKII.js
```

Conclusion: We should remove the `invalidateModule` in the transform hook because it impacts CCTs and it seems to never run. Even if it runs rare occasions, it's more important to enable CCTs to work rather than HMR in rare circumstances.

If someone can give me a reproduction of when QRLs don't get updated on parent change, I can reassess and try to find a fix that works both for CCTs and HMR.

body: ## 📣 Related Issue - close #300 ## 📝 Summary - [x] 툴 상세 정보에서 북마크 여부가 정상적으로 반환되지 않는 문제를 해결 - [x] Presigned URL을 요청할 때, `body`가 아닌, `parameter`를 통해서 요청하도록 변경 ## 🙏 Question & PR point - `JwtAuthenticationFilter`를 거치지 않는 API는 인증 객체가 존재하지 않기 때문에, `@AuthenticationPrincipal`을 통해서 `userId`를 가지고 올 수 없습니다. 이번 오류도 해당 이슈로 인해서 발생하여 수정하였습니다. - `GET` 요청의 경우에는 Body를 통해 요청이 불가한 것으로 알고 있습니다. 따라서 이를 해결하기 위해 query parameter를 통해서 요청하도록 변경합니다. ## 📬 Postman ### 툴 상세 정보에서 북마크 여부가 정상적으로 반환되지 않는 문제를 해결 ### Presigned URL을 요청할 때, `body`가 아닌, `parameter`를 통해서 요청하도록 변경 #### | 위의 결과로 업로드한 이미지를 아래에 첨부 합니다. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **기능 개선** * presigned URL 발급 API가 단일 이미지 이름을 쿼리 파라미터로 받아 단일 URL을 반환하도록 변경되었습니다. * 툴 상세 조회 시 인증이 필수로 적용되어, 해당 API 호출 시 토큰 인증이 필요합니다. * 툴 목록 조회 시 필터링, 정렬, 페이징 로직이 서버 내부에서 효율적으로 처리되도록 개선되었습니다. * **API 변경** * presigned URL 요청 방식이 JSON body에서 쿼리 파라미터(imageName)로 변경되었습니다. * presigned URL 응답이 리스트가 아닌 단일 문자열 URL로 변경되었습니다. * **기타** * 일부 파라미터 명칭이 일관성 있게 수정되었습니다. * Swagger 설정에서 서버 URL이 고정값으로 변경되어, 개발 및 운영 서버 정보가 명확해졌습니다. * Sentry 설정에서 불필요한 server-uri 속성이 제거되었습니다.

author: elizamkraule
body:
Backport 1/1 commits from #148753.

/cc @cockroachdb/release

---

A recent change added detailed logging for Kafka v2 changefeed
messages that exceed the broker's size limit. These logs now
include the message key, size, and MVCC timestamp to aid in
debugging.

To make this safe for backporting, the behavior is now gated
behind the cluster setting:

changefeed.kafka_v2_include_error_details

In the main branch, this setting defaults to true to preserve
the enhanced observability.

In release branch backports, it will default to false.

When enabled, the log will include:
- The key of the offending message
- Combined key + value size
- MVCC timestamp

When disabled, the log reverts to the previous, minimal format.

Related to: 
Jira issue: [CRDB-49646](https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/browse/CRDB-49646)
See also #144994


Release note (general change): Kafka v2 changefeed sinks now
support a cluster setting that enables detailed error logging
for messages exceeding Kafka v2 size limit.

body:
Currently a mei file like this:
```
 <score>
          <scoreDef>
            <staffGrp>
              <staffDef n="1" lines="5" meter.count="4" meter.unit="4">
                <clef shape="G" line="2" />
              </staffDef>
            </staffGrp>
          </scoreDef>
          <section>
            <measure n="1">
              <staff n="1">
                <layer n="1">
                  <note dur="4" pname="c" oct="4" />
                  <note dur="4" pname="d" oct="4" />
                  <note dur="4" pname="e" oct="4" />
                  <note dur="4" pname="f" oct="4" />
                </layer>
              </staff>
            </measure>
          </section>
        </score>
```

produces these warnings:
```
Warning, replacing existing token: 4d with a null token around time 1/4 in layerindex 0
GRID STAFF: (v0:) "4e"  [] 
Warning, replacing existing token: 4e with a null token around time 1/4 in layerindex 0
GRID STAFF: (v0:) "4f"  [] 
Warning, replacing existing token: 4f with a null token around time 1/4 in layerindex 0
GRID STAFF: (v0:) ".ZZZ4e"  [] 
Warning, replacing existing token: .ZZZ4e with a null token around time 1/4 in layerindex 0
GRID STAFF: (v0:) ".ZZZ4f"  [] 
Warning, replacing existing token: .ZZZ4f with a null token around time 1 in layerindex 0
GRID STAFF: (v0:) ".ZZZ4f"  [] 
Warning, replacing existing token: .ZZZ4f with a null token around time 1 in layerindex 0
```

and the humdrum output gets tagged with ZZZ: 
```
!!!OTL: Test
**kern
*part1
*staff1
*M4/4
4c
.ZZZ4d
.ZZZ4e
.ZZZ4f
=
*-
```

The problem seems to be that `tool-mei2hum.cpp` defines `QUARTER_CONVERT` as no-op, resulting on wrong duration for measures parsed from mei files. Uncommenting the original `#define QUARTER_CONVERT * 4` fixes the issue.

author: axelson
body:
Refresh session tokens after they expire in an hour

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/authconcept.html#sessionsconcept

Based on this doc: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/authconcept.html#sessionsconcept
Depending on the configured expiration time for the `aws sso login` token which can be up to 90 days, the "application session" token (which I presume is what you're using in the batch process) only receives tokens that are valid for 1 hour (I assume this is a security measure so the session can be revoked without waiting a full 90 days).

So how do you refresh the tokens, you make a `CreateToken` call: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/OIDCAPIReference/API_CreateToken.html

Here's the base url: "https://oidc.#{region}.amazonaws.com/token"

And here's an example of the payload (where the `sso_cache` is from `~/.aws/sso/cache`):
```
payload = %{
  "grantType" => "refresh_token",
  "clientId" => sso_cache["clientId"],
  "clientSecret" => sso_cache["clientSecret"],
  "refreshToken" => sso_cache["refreshToken"]
}
```

TODO:
- Clean up so it can be upstreamed (improve expiration detection)
- Should we be writing the updated token back into the cache?

This PR refactors the complex Zenn MCP server into a simplified, FastMCP-based implementation focused solely on feed retrieval functionality.

## Key Changes
- **Architecture Migration**: Traditional MCP → FastMCP (50% code reduction)
- **Feature Simplification**: Removed AI summarization, report generation, and complex filtering
- **Dependency Optimization**: Removed Google Cloud AI Platform and related dependencies
- **Code Quality**: Improved maintainability and test coverage

## Features Removed
- ❌ AI summarization functionality (`summarizer.py`)
- ❌ Markdown report generation (`renderer.py`)  
- ❌ Vertex AI integration (`vertex_ai_client.py`)
- ❌ Complex MCP tools (`get_article_summary`, `save_report`)
- ❌ Period filtering (incomplete implementation)
- ❌ Like count sorting (unavailable from feed)

## Features Retained
- ✅ Zenn topic feed retrieval
- ✅ Basic article information (title, url, published_at, description)
- ✅ Article count limiting (1-10 articles)
- ✅ Error handling and structured logging

## Technical Improvements
- **Code Reduction**: `main.py` (164→81 lines), `crawler.py` (173→90 lines)
- **Configuration**: Simplified from 18 to 3 settings (83% reduction)
- **Tests**: Optimized from 22 to 17 test cases, all passing
- **Dependencies**: Removed ~30 unused packages

## Documentation Updates
- Updated `requirements.md` to reflect current implementation
- Added comprehensive development log (`docs/dev_log/`)
- Created SOW for the simplified feature (`docs/sow/`)

## Test Results
- ✅ All 17 tests passing
- ✅ FastMCP functionality verified
- ✅ Error handling tested
- ✅ Input validation confirmed

## Performance Impact
- ⚡ Significantly faster startup (no AI model loading)
- ⚡ Reduced memory footprint
- ⚡ Simplified error paths
- ⚡ Faster dependency installation

## Breaking Changes
- MCP tool interface simplified (removed unused parameters)
- Response format streamlined to essential information only

author: ydwu4
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #158273

Before the PR, for code like this:
```
        class Example2(torch.nn.Module):
            def forward(self, x, trigger, target):
                return torch.cond(
                    trigger == 1,
                    lambda: x + target,
                    lambda: x * target,
                    (),
                )

        m = Example2()
        x = torch.randn(2)
        trigger = 0
        target = 2
        args = (x, trigger, target)
        ep = torch.export.export(
            m, args, dynamic_shapes=(None, Dim.DYNAMIC, Dim.DYNAMIC)
        )
```
dynamo will wrap "target" (i.e. a symInt) twice, once when we speculate the first lambda and find target is a symint and decides to wrap it up, creating a new SymNodeVariable and a placeholder input to the top-level graph.

The second time happens when we speculate the second lambda. Tensors are de-duplicated by checking tracked side effects to make sure object with the same id (though different sources) is mapped to the same TensorVaraible. For symints, two things are missing:
1. it's not in the _can_lift_attrs_to_input list (the change in builder.py)
2. it's not in the tracked by runahead_side_effects, so when speculate_subgraph finishes, they're discarded (the change in side_effects.py)

Note: the auto lifting mechanism for HOPs happens at proxy level when we trace the subgraph, which is after SymNodeVariable are created (they're created when realizing the args and bind them to subgraph). At that time, builder has created two unique SymNodeVariable for the same symint so the auto lifting in hops cannot de-dup them.

author: c-loftus
body:
Experiment changing the crawl stats to be formatted as jsonld.

I have mixed opinions on this. Since this jsonld is essentially being used as a source of truth for our future crawl status frontend, it is unclear if adding jsonld properties to this actually just makes it harder to work with. We aren't including this data in our final triplestore, and it is only for internal use so I am not sure if it is worth it. That is since the report has a few properties which don't fit into a preexisting vocab well; defining a new vocabulary is always possible, but defining ad hoc vocabs seem to greatly reduce their utility.

body:
Fixes [SENTRY-441R](https://sentry.io/organizations/sentry/issues/6714039058/). The issue was that: Database-level `on_delete=SET_NULL` cascade on `sentry_grouphashmetadata` generates an unbatched, large `UPDATE` query, causing `QueryCanceled` and `ProcessingDeadlineExceeded`.

- Avoids a massive UPDATE query when deleting GroupHash by setting `seer_matched_grouphash_id` to NULL in batches.


This fix was generated by Seer in Sentry, triggered by Armen Zambrano Gasparnian. 👁️ Run ID: 345746

author: dhirmadi
body:
## 🐛 Problem

SuperAdmin authentication and UI display issues were caused by a race condition between Auth0 authentication and React Query API calls. The application was making API requests before authentication tokens were available, resulting in:

- 401 errors during initial page load
- SuperAdmin features not displaying correctly
- Poor user experience with error flashes before successful authentication

## 🔧 Solution

### Core Changes

1. **Enhanced AuthContext with `isReady` State**
   - Added `isReady` boolean that indicates when authentication is complete AND ready for API calls
   - Combines `isAuthenticated && !auth0Loading && !rolesLoading && roles !== null`
   - Provides proper coordination between Auth0 and React Query

2. **Updated All React Query Hooks**
   - Modified `useTenants`, `useProjects`, `useCloudProviders`, `useProjectTypes`, `useFiles` hooks
   - Added `enabled: isReady` to prevent premature API calls
   - Fixed import paths to use correct AuthContext location

3. **Enhanced ProtectedRoute Component**
   - Updated to check both `isLoading` and `!isReady` before allowing route access
   - Shows loading spinner until authentication is fully complete
   - Better user experience during authentication process

4. **Improved User Experience**
   - Added `AuthLoadingSpinner` component for consistent loading states
   - Enhanced error handling and logging for development
   - Eliminated error flashes during initial authentication

### Technical Details

- **Race Condition Resolution**: API calls now wait for Auth0 token availability
- **Type Safety**: All changes maintain TypeScript strict mode compliance
- **Performance**: No unnecessary API calls during authentication process
- **Debugging**: Enhanced logging for development troubleshooting

## ✅ Testing

- [x] Build completes successfully with no TypeScript errors
- [x] All hooks properly coordinate with authentication state
- [x] No more 401 errors during initial page load
- [x] SuperAdmin features display correctly after authentication
- [x] Loading states provide good user experience

## 📋 Files Changed

- `src/core/context/AuthContext.tsx` - Added isReady state and coordination logic
- `src/core/router/ProtectedRoute.tsx` - Enhanced loading state handling
- `src/features/*/hooks/*.ts` - Updated all hooks to wait for auth readiness
- `src/shared/components/AuthLoadingSpinner.tsx` - New loading component

## 🔄 Impact

This change completely resolves the SuperAdmin authentication issues by ensuring proper coordination between Auth0 authentication and React Query data fetching. Users will now see consistent loading states instead of error messages during the authentication process.

## 🚀 Next Steps

- Monitor authentication flow in production
- Consider adding authentication state persistence for better UX
- Evaluate opportunities for further performance optimization

author: justinhandley
body:
This pull request enhances the SDK generator by integrating Prisma's DMMF (Data Model Meta Format) for better model parsing and introduces separate admin GraphQL files with a customizable prefix. The changes improve flexibility and maintainability in handling Prisma models and GraphQL schema generation.

### Prisma DMMF Integration:
* Added `getDMMF` from `@prisma/internals` to parse Prisma models with support for documentation comments. This replaces the previous `parsePrismaModels` approach. (`generators/shared/src/sdk/generator.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a221315742dafa604b029859334610195e71b0016d7416572659c16bf5f687c2R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a221315742dafa604b029859334610195e71b0016d7416572659c16bf5f687c2L142-R181)

### Admin GraphQL Files Generation:
* Introduced a new helper function, `getAdminFragmentFields`, to generate admin-specific fragment fields for models. (`generators/shared/src/sdk/generator.ts`, [generators/shared/src/sdk/generator.tsR72-R95](diffhunk://#diff-a221315742dafa604b029859334610195e71b0016d7416572659c16bf5f687c2R72-R95))
* Added logic to generate admin GraphQL files in a separate directory (`libs/shared/sdk/src/admin-graphql`) with an optional `Admin` prefix for fragments, mutations, and queries. (`generators/shared/src/sdk/generator.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a221315742dafa604b029859334610195e71b0016d7416572659c16bf5f687c2L163-R233) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a221315742dafa604b029859334610195e71b0016d7416572659c16bf5f687c2R242-L174)

### Template Updates for GraphQL Files:
* Updated GraphQL templates (`__name__-fragments.graphql__tmpl__`, `__name__-mutations.graphql__tmpl__`, `__name__-queries.graphql__tmpl__`) to include the `adminPrefix` for admin-specific operations. (`generators/shared/src/sdk/graphql/__name__-fragments.graphql__tmpl__`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-396cee1e12a30f42934b99015c082db9f77ef7ea67567c2b4b33fd8020a0ebe9L1-R7); `__name__-mutations.graphql__tmpl__`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50dbba2822bb75f645676ff80dcf2ceba31ede85f30207b5d6dfc9997b4b3d10L1-R15); `__name__-queries.graphql__tmpl__`, [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2c4d5da129de6c67a90c525fcf7875faa720ad871a627c753b0ee8748b57a29aL1-R16)

### Code Refinements:
* Enhanced the logic for generating fragment fields by filtering out unnecessary fields like `id`, `Id`-suffixed fields, and non-scalar types. (`generators/shared/src/sdk/generator.ts`, [generators/shared/src/sdk/generator.tsL163-R233](diffhunk://#diff-a221315742dafa604b029859334610195e71b0016d7416572659c16bf5f687c2L163-R233))
* Adjusted step numbering in comments to reflect the new workflow. (`generators/shared/src/sdk/generator.ts`, [generators/shared/src/sdk/generator.tsL184-R262](diffhunk://#diff-a221315742dafa604b029859334610195e71b0016d7416572659c16bf5f687c2L184-R262))

**Describe your changes**
Update within `pcv.homology.acute` to turn off print statements with `pcv.params.verbose`, rather than controlling the print statements by changing debug mode to `None`. With these proposed changes, a user can create a debugging image without necessarily printing out many lines of statements.  

**Type of update**
Is this a:
* code cleanup 

**Associated issues**
- closes #1729 

**Additional context**
It seems like there's mention of a `verbose` text file, which I think it aims to capture the print statements in a text file rather than printing to the screen. Not implemented currently; it's unclear to me how these print statements help with debugging but I would be happy to make the verbose text file work if someone would find it helpful.

author: pjohnst5
body:
# CNS IBDevice API Contracts

## Overview
Two new APIs for managing InfiniBand (IB) devices in Azure Container Network Service (CNS):

1. **POST IB Devices for Pod** - POST IB devices for a pod
2. **GET IB Device Info** - GET IB device status

---

## API 1: POST IB Devices for Pod

### Endpoint
```
POST /ibdevices
```

### Request Body
```json

{
  "ibmacaddresses": [
    "60:45:bd:a4:b5:7a",
    "7c:1e:52:07:11:36"
  ],
  "podNamespace": "default",
  "podName": "example-pod"
}
```

### Success Response
```json
{
  "message": "Successfully assigned 2 devices to pod my-pod-my-namespace"
}
```

### Error Response
`HTTP 400`
```json
{
  "message": "Device 60:45:bd:a4:b5:7a is already assigned to another pod"
}
```
---

## API 2: GET IB Device Information

### Endpoint
```
GET /ibdevices?ibmac=60:45:bd:a4:b5:7a
```

### Request
No request body (MAC address provided as query param)

### Success Response
```json
{
  "ibMACAddress": "60:45:bd:a4:b5:7a",
  "podNamespace": "mynamespace",
  "podName": "mypod", 
  "status": "programmingComplete",
  "message": ""
}
```

### Device Not Found Response
`HTTP 404`
```json
{
  "ibMACAddress": "60:45:bd:a4:b5:7a",
  "podNamespace": "",
  "podName": "", 
  "message": "Device not found"
}
```

See `status.go` in this PR for list of all statuses of an IB device

---

## Request body
See `api.go` for the structs
- `AssignIBDevicesToPodRequest`
- `AssignIBDevicesToPodResponse`
- `GetIBDeviceInfoResponse`

You can also do multi searches by placing them in { } curly braces and separated by either ( , or | ) a comma will be treated as AND in the search while a pipe ( | ) will be treated as OR

example: {hp>=500, ac<=100} this will return items with hp values of 500 and up, and ac values of 100 and below

example: {name~"words of" | name~"rune of"} will find items with either "words of" or "rune of" in the name

author: eportman
body:
Issue Number: https://github.com/bcgov/entity/issues/29305

Add in Scalar OAS3 doc for namex api.

This still needs quite a bit more work before it is stable. Some changes also need to happen to the actual API itself to support this smoothly. 

Mainly being:
  - Creating an NR and generating the nr invoice is flakey and doesn't seem to be fully supported by using an api client alone
  - Returning the correct status codes for the endpoints (404 when not found not just a blanket 400 or 500, etc.)
  - A lot of the endpoints requires the `Bcreg-Nrl` in the header even though it is almost never used, if it is not sent as an empty string a lot of endpoints return a 500 making the whole thing confusing
  - Other quirks that will come up when this gets tested

author: arifthpe
body:
Previously we relied on system LLVM (11) on Amazon Linux 2, as the default GCC is too old to build LLVM. However, after dropping support for LLVM 11 in https://github.com/chapel-lang/chapel/pull/27326, this is no longer an option. Update the build process for Amazon Linux 2 to install the available `gcc10` package, and set `CC` and `CXX` so it will be used during Chapel build. Also update `prereqs.rst` to reflect this.

Additionally, since this will enable building with `CHPL_LLVM=none`, add a `-nollvm` variant of the `amazonlinux-2` apptainer portability testing configuration.

While here, update the path to the `extract-docs.py` script referenced in `prereqs.rst`, which was moved in https://github.com/chapel-lang/chapel/pull/27398.

- [x] locally testing LLVM and no-LLVM configs (in Docker) works

1. removed need for home_score or away_score in Game class

author: chrisrueger
body: the new bnd manual generator was randomly throwing a exception, because the `bnd.createOptions` contained two 'manifest' options, one lowercased `manifest()` one Capitalized `Manifest()` and violates the rule in the comment below that the first 3 characters must not be the same (`3+ throw an error) ` https://github.com/bndtools/bnd/blob/6e0b150b13324e425e4d1deedaedbd42bd7f6bed/aQute.libg/src/aQute/lib/getopt/CommandLine.java#L401-L409 Depending on the mood of the jvm in which it returns `Class.getMethods()` sometimes it will get Manifest() first and sometimes the lowercase version. In the map of options only the lowercase letter is used (-m) but with the method of the uppercase method. Clearly random and messed up. Since the user only sees the lowercase `-m` version, it also means that the other one is currently swallowed and not usable. I renamed it to `skipmanifest`, because I think this createOptions violates what the exception is telling us and is also confusingly named IMO. And `skipmanifest` seems not wrong. ``` Errors 000: Exception: java.lang.Error: Only commands with lower case first char are acceptable (Manifest) at aQute.lib.getopt.CommandLine.getOptions(CommandLine.java:408) at aQute.lib.getopt.CommandLine.generateDocumentationForCommand(CommandLine.java:206) at aQute.bnd.main.ManualGenerator.generateCommandsFiles(ManualGenerator.java:90) at aQute.bnd.main.bnd._generatemanual(bnd.java:1286) ``` Now the command help `bnd help create` reads: ``` NAME create - Equivalent jar command c[v0mf] command (supports the jar tool's syntax). Will wrap the bundle unless --wrapnot is specified SYNOPSIS create [options] ... OPTIONS [ -b, --bsn ] - Bundle Symbolic Name for wrap [ -c, --cdir ] - directory [ -f, --file ] - Jar file (f option) [ -F, --force ] - Force write event if there are errors [ -m, --manifest ] - Use manifest (m option) [ -n, --nocompression ] - No compression (0 option) [ -p, --properties ] - Properties for wrapping [ -s, --skipmanifest ] - No manifest. [ -v, --verbose ] - Verbose (v option) [ -V, --version ] - Bundle Version for wrap [ -w, --wrap ] - Wrap ```

## Summary

Updates the logger package documentation to accurately reflect the unified API implementation completed in issue #53. The previous documentation contained outdated API signatures and incorrect environment limitations.

## Changes Made

### API Reference Documentation (`docs/packages/logger/api-reference.md`)
- Updated all method signatures from `(msg: string, ...args: Array<unknown>)` to `(message: string, context?: LogContext)`
- Removed incorrect claims that `withTag()` and `withContext()` only work in browser environments
- Updated factory function documentation to reflect unified `createLogger()` working in all environments
- Added comprehensive documentation for new testing utilities (`createMockLogger`, `createCapturingMockLogger`)
- Updated TypeScript interface definitions to match unified implementation
- Added deprecation notice for `createCliLogger()` with migration guidance

### Architecture Documentation (`docs/packages/logger/architecture.md`)
- Updated Node.js implementation details to show unified API support
- Added documentation for `withTag()` and `withContext()` methods in Node.js
- Updated testing section to highlight built-in testing utilities
- Added deprecation notice for CLI logger variant
- Updated context merging examples to use proper TypeScript types

## Key Improvements

- **API Consistency**: All documentation now reflects the unified `(message, context?)` signature across environments
- **Environment Parity**: Removed false claims about browser-only features
- **Testing Support**: Comprehensive documentation for new built-in testing utilities
- **Migration Guidance**: Clear deprecation notices with recommended alternatives
- **Type Safety**: Updated all TypeScript interfaces to use proper `LogContext` type

## Validation

The documentation now accurately reflects:
- Unified logger API from issue #53 implementation
- Testing utilities available in `packages/logger/src/lib/testing.ts`
- Migration guide patterns from `packages/logger/src/lib/migration-guide.ts`
- Consistent behavior across Node.js and browser environments

## Test plan

- [x] Review updated API signatures match actual implementation
- [x] Verify testing utility documentation is accurate
- [x] Confirm environment limitation claims are removed
- [x] Check TypeScript interface consistency

author: nkeke21
body:
Updated event-related endpoints to use session-based authentication.
The backend now determines the event host from the currently authenticated user in the session, rather than relying on data from the frontend. This improves security and ensures that only the logged-in user can create or modify events as the host.
Key changes:

- Event creation and update endpoints now set the host using the session user.
- The frontend no longer sends or controls the hostId.
- Ensures all event actions are properly tied to the authenticated user.

author: placerda
body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the project, including a shift to a containerized development environment, enhancements to the application's telemetry and configuration management, and a streamlined deployment process. The changes aim to improve developer experience, simplify deployment, and enhance observability.

### Containerization and Development Environment:

* Added a `Dockerfile` to define the application environment, leveraging `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:dev-3.12` as the base image, and exposing port 80 for application access. (`Dockerfile`, [DockerfileR1-R21](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557R1-R21))
* Introduced a `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` file to set up a development container with pre-installed tools like Git and Azure CLI, and configured VS Code settings for Python debugging.

### Telemetry and Configuration Management:

* Replaced environment variable-based configuration with a centralized `get_config` dependency, enabling structured access to application settings across modules. (`app.py`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959R11-R19); `auth.py`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-dbcf43432c07570656f9b214353e5df97b86882c0e6da4bc037be69c25c52174R9-R21)
* Integrated OpenTelemetry for tracing, including attributes like `message_id` and `conversation_id` in spans for better observability. (`app.py`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959L88-R76) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959R89-R92)

### Deployment Process:

* Updated `azure.yaml` to include infrastructure provisioning via Bicep templates and added predeploy hooks for both Windows and POSIX systems. (`azure.yaml`, [azure.yamlL1-R21](diffhunk://#diff-1ba5bd52036276068bc787a1be3dfa49aa920317ab02fa460c99246a78e588f3L1-R21))
* Simplified deployment instructions in `README.md`, replacing manual environment variable setup with `azd env refresh` and `azd deploy` commands. (`README.md`, [README.mdL1-R53](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L1-R53))

### Removal of Legacy Code:

* Removed `.env.template`, `app_settings.json`, and `.vscode/settings.json` files, which previously contained environment variable definitions and deployment configurations. (`.env.template`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-749e06f64632f62a0c0dfbf4c4f3850e27e94ac109aa121fabd5c29469ae88deL1-L67); `app_settings.json`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ddb3dd617bdcf1392a251e0a2ec6488889437e9b9cb63fab2b2e246d655a7093L1-L103); `.vscode/settings.json`, [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a5de3e5871ffcc383a2294845bd3df25d3eeff6c29ad46e3a396577c413bf357L1-L4)

### Minor Enhancements:

* Updated `connectors/__init__.py` to include `AppConfigClient` for improved configuration management. (`connectors/__init__.py`, [connectors/__init__.pyR3](diffhunk://#diff-fab4cab78bd8cd4dc415a3675fec2ef317ff4289f83501c32467ca47a947ea54R3))
* Adjusted FastAPI debugging configuration in `.vscode/launch.json` to use port 80 and added environment variables for application configuration. (`.vscode/launch.json`, [.vscode/launch.jsonL5-R18](diffhunk://#diff-bd5430ee7c51dc892a67b3f2829d1f5b6d223f0fd48b82322cfd45baf9f5e945L5-R18))

author: keithamus
body:
def.rs was getting a little unweildy, as it was over 1kLOC. This aims to break it up a bit by separating the two responsibilities: 

- def.rs is now responsible for defining the types, and parsing the CSS type definition grammaer into Defs.
- generate.rs is now responsible for taking a Def and generating Rust data structures, such as the struct/enums, as well as the necessary variants & types.

In moving them over, I've also spent a bit of time cleaning the code. Some various wins:

- The ToType trait now generates a list of types that each Def corresponds to. The old code for this used to couple variant names and the inner types, but that's been massively simplified so that ToType can be relied on to get a list of types and nothing more.
- ToType also has a `to_singular_type()` which will return either the single type or the tuple of the types, which makes it easier to use this type both inside of struct/enums but also as peek/parse steps.
- The ToField trait now encapsulates the variant/member name logic.
- We're using `CommaSeparated<T>` now for `OneOrMoreCommaSeparated` which is a tiny bit cleaner.

Some things still todo:

- I'm sure more parse/peek steps can be simplified. 
- I haven't yet got codegen working for `Optionals!` as it's tricky due to the keyword stuff. We should look at this more.

author: turbolent
body:
Work toward #4059 

## Description

- Rename the `new` instruction to `newComposite` to make it clearer that only composite values can be allocated with the instruction
- Add a new instruction `newCompositeAt` which is the same as `newComposite`, but it has an address operand. `newComposite` is now an optimization for a very common case
- Emit `newCompositeAt` instead of `newComposite` when allocating the composite value in a contract initializer of a contract deployed to an address location. This creates the composite value immediately in the account, like the interpreter does. Currently the value was allocated on the stack (address 0x0) and the writes were lost
- Implement the `newCompositeAt` instruction in the VM: It has the same behaviour as `newComposite`, but the given address is used instead of the implicit zero address
- Add a dedicated test case for compiling contracts with initializers. This was so far only tested implicitly/partially through other tests
- Enable both failing test cases which now work as expected

author: djmrfunnyman
body: Fixes #1559 ## Description: The current Mars map has several issues: - The map is very underdetailed - The coastlines are very smooth and visually unappealing - The map was created from an incompatible source image, which results in the height data being very wrong - As a result the map hardly resembles Mars at all. - There is too much land - The major landmass is almost entirely covered in plains - The ocean doesn't match the heightmap - The gameplay is boring - The map is very succeptable to snowballing issues - The map seems commonly disliked in the community I attempted to remedy this. - The water level and elevation are calculated from accurate height data - Water level is much higher making the map much more interesting, both in the gameplay and visual aspect. - The map has several contitents which should slow down snowballing - The map is much more detailed overall - I added a lot more NPC's. 8 for such a big map just wasn't enough. - [x] I have added screenshots for all UI updates - [x] I process any text displayed to the user through translateText() and I've added it to the en.json file - [x] I have added relevant tests to the test directory - [x] I confirm I have thoroughly tested these changes and take full responsibility for any bugs introduced - [x] I understand that submitting code with bugs that could have been caught through manual testing blocks releases and new features for all contributors ## Please put your Discord username so you can be contacted if a bug or regression is found: aceralex

Add a `per-region` template that provisions all the Resources (such as VPC, NAT, Subnets, etc.) need in an AWS Region to support deploying one or more Marketing Site Stacks in that Account Region. Expand the list of supported Regions to all non-gov US Regions and use a consistent set of IP address ranges within each VPC.

Continues the work of #66824

Successfully provisioned multiple Marketing Sites in multiple Regions in #67090

## Description
- Split up code into more organized components, CalenderEvents, RecommendedEvents, MyEvent, and EventCard
- Calendar Events: Create separate component and changed so it auto displays the current day's events
- Event Card: Created separate component for code cleanness 
- Events: Updated events component to just simply handle the change of the views the user can have on the page, which are Calendar View, Recommended Events, and My Events.
- My Events: Added "My Events" toggle so users can view the events they have already RSVP'd for
- Recommended Events: Added similar display to "My Events" but it just fetches the scored upcoming events and just displays the top 5 weighted score events.
- Updated scoreEvents route to display each events information with the score given

## Milestones
- Wrapping up Technical Challenge 1

## Resources
- Stack Overflow 

## Test Plan
- Visually tested and confirmed the new components setup was properly working like using the site and toggling around the events page to different views confirmation everything worked
- Made sure updated return of event information for scoreEvents properly displayed with Insomnia

https://www.loom.com/share/24941d8507644bbabcaccad8f0cba15f?sid=c3d30e5b-30be-444f-842b-de180a5d7ccc

- Noticed in the video with the event that has passed by the time but it was schedule for today, was still showing on recommended events but when I checked for it to display in my upcoming events it didn't like how it should since its for upcoming events and not in the day view. So I need to go back and change so it only displays recommended events that are in the future (in time).

### Description

The current `--with-vitest` example's root vitest.config.ts has `*` in the paths which seems to be invalid as shown below:

```
The project root contains the "*" character (/workspace/tmp/my-turborepo/packages/*), which may not work when running Vite. Consider renaming the directory / file to remove the characters.
The project root contains the "*" character (/workspace/tmp/my-turborepo/apps/*), which may not work when running Vite. Consider renaming the directory / file to remove the characters.

 DEV  v3.2.4 /workspace/tmp/my-turborepo

No test files found. You can change the file name pattern by pressing "p"


 0  

include: **/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)
exclude:  **/node_modules/**, **/dist/**, **/cypress/**, **/.{idea,git,cache,output,temp}/**, **/{karma,rollup,webpack,vite,vitest,jest,ava,babel,nyc,cypress,tsup,build,eslint,prettier}.config.*

 1  

include: **/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)
exclude:  **/node_modules/**, **/dist/**, **/cypress/**, **/.{idea,git,cache,output,temp}/**, **/{karma,rollup,webpack,vite,vitest,jest,ava,babel,nyc,cypress,tsup,build,eslint,prettier}.config.*
```

Removing `/*` sufix fixes this issue as show below:

```
› bun run test:projects:watch
$ vitest --watch

 DEV  v3.2.4 /workspace/tmp/my-turborepo

 ✓  0  math/tests/math.test.ts (2 tests) 2ms
 ✓  1  web/tests/math.test.ts (1 test) 1ms
 ✓  1  docs/tests/math.test.ts (1 test) 1ms

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
   Start at  07:11:36
   Duration  515ms (transform 43ms, setup 0ms, collect 31ms, tests 4ms, environment 626ms, prepare 139ms)
```

This is related to https://github.com/vercel/turborepo/issues/10659#event-18621158590

### Testing Instructions

Just run:

`bun run test:projects:watch`

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Introduced comprehensive SDK libraries for compressed token operations, including account management, batch compression, delegation, freezing, minting, and transfer instructions.
  * Added extensive Solana program modules and test suites for compressed token workflows, such as deposit, escrow, batch operations, and multi-invocation flows.
  * Provided new utility functions for deriving token pool addresses and managing account metadata.
  * Added detailed documentation and debugging guides for CPI context and token operations.

* **Improvements**
  * Standardized naming and data structures for compressed token accounts across SDK and client libraries.
  * Enhanced error handling with custom error types and numeric codes for SDK operations.
  * Updated client and indexer APIs to consistently use compressed token account representations.
  * Improved account info management and configuration for cross-program invocations.
  * Refined trait bounds and ownership semantics for account info handling in CPI contexts.
  * Added explicit error handling for system account additions to prevent silent failures.
  * Optimized CPI invocation code by removing unnecessary cloning of account infos.

* **Tests**
  * Added comprehensive integration and unit tests covering compression, transfer, decompression, batch operations, deposit flows, and multi-invocation scenarios.

* **Documentation**
  * Added in-depth guides and references for debugging and implementing compressed token operations, including CPI context best practices.

* **Chores**
  * Updated workspace configuration to integrate new SDK libraries and test programs.
  * Refactored code for consistency, visibility, and trait bounds where necessary.
  * Reorganized imports and code structure for clarity and maintainability.
